From microplastics clogging up our oceans to landfills leaching out dangerous chemicals, plastic waste is a serious and growing problem for human health and the environment. We need to recycle more, and crucially, recycle better.

Most plastic that is recycled is melted and remoulded into lower-quality products such as carpet fibres and garden planters, before eventually ending up in landfill or the incinerator. This is downcycling rather than proper recycling. Current methods don’t enable the recovery of the original components of the waste – that means they cannot be truly recycled back into new high-quality plastic.

open image in gallery Most plastic that is recycled is melted and remoulded into lower-quality products such as carpet fibres and garden planters ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

A 2026 study from the University of Manchester marks a potential turning point in our ability to recycle better. The study focused on polycarbonate, a type of hard plastic. These plastics are common, but notoriously difficult to degrade as they are specifically designed for strength and durability for use in safety glasses, electronics and as machine parts.

The Manchester authors report a way to rapidly digest polycarbonate back to its original building blocks. They did this by creating an enzyme (proteins that carry out chemical reactions) to digest the polycarbonate. This is part of a major emerging field, using super-enzymes for green recycling of our waste.

Enzymes are nature’s nano-machines, they speed up reactions to make and break chemical bonds, converting one compound into another. For example, digestive enzymes can break starch in bread back to the simple sugars from which it is made. If enzymes could similarly digest plastic into its original building blocks these blocks could then be re-used to synthesise new plastic. So, a double win, less waste, plus this could drastically decrease the need to extract crude oil to manufacture new plastic.

However, there are two big problems. First, plastics need heating to around 70°C to open up their structures enough for the enzymes to get at the chemical bonds that hold them together. But enzymes are proteins, and proteins get destroyed by heat, think of the way the clear protein in your egg white solidifies and permanently changes as it hits the pan. The other issue is that enzymes have evolved to work on natural compounds, not human-made synthetics.

Ancient evolution can help with the heat problem. Some microbes, called extremophiles, live at temperatures of more than 100°C, in volcanoes and deep-sea hot springs. To be able to do this, their proteins have evolved special features to make them thermo-resistant. These include a rigid outer shell, and lots of high-strength bonds between different parts of the protein, acting like steel girders to reinforce the structure against the effects of heat. These evolutionary innovations give us a blueprint for making our plastic digesters heat-resistant.

That still leaves the difficulty of how to get enzymes to work on synthetic materials. Here we can turn to some of the tricks used by protein engineers like me. One approach is directed evolution, a way of breeding better proteins by repeated mutation and selection, just like natural evolution but compressing that process in the lab into just a few weeks. Directed evolution can train proteins to work on plastics rather than their natural substrates, and this was a key method employed by the Manchester group in their development of a polycarbonate digester.

Supercharging with AI

Artificial intelligence can supercharge the process of protein and enzyme design. By training machine learning models to analyse millions of existing proteins, correlations between the specific functional activity of each protein and the structural features that make up that protein can be mapped. The computer can then predict what structural features we need to introduce or modify in our starting protein to achieve a particular target function.

About the author Nick Brindle is a Professor of Cell Signalling, University of Leicester. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Combining strategies like directed evolution and AI, and adding the hacks for heat resistance learned from the extremophiles, lets scientists build super-enzymes, stable at 70°C and trained to digest plastics and spit out the very components needed to make a truly circular plastic economy.

Using super-enzymes for green recycling is on the horizon for other types of waste as well, including synthetic textiles, electronics and even astronaut waste deep in space. By looking back to ancient evolution and combining this with the latest lab evolution and AI we could improve our future, potentially changing plastic waste from a problem into a resource.

ESPN fans have raged against the company’s most recent round of layoffs that axed several of the network’s mainstays.

MLB announcer Karl Ravech, NFL MVP Cam Newton, longtime SportsCenter anchor David Lloyd, injury analyst Stephania Bell, former All-Pro linebacker and studio host Bart Scott and NFL Network analyst Charles Davis have all reportedly been impacted.

A 31-year veteran of the network, Ravech served as ESPN’s lead MLB play-by-play announcer, covered college basketball and anchored SportsCenter. He called the Dodgers-Phillies game Monday before reportedly learning his position was in jeopardy. When contacted by The Athletic Tuesday, 61-year-old Ravech said he had not yet been informed of his status.

Fans were furious to learn of Ravech’s fate, with one writing on X: “ESPN laid off Karl Ravech one month before the Little League World Series. Shameful. He was as good as it gets for that event, and another part of my childhood is no more.”

“I watched Karl Ravech host Baseball Tonight every night as a kid. 10 pm sharp. I loved the game and relished the highlights. He was a true pro. That era of ESPN, and sports coverage in general, is long gone,” another lamented.

Karl Ravech, pictured, is reportedly among those impacted by ESPN’s latest round of layoffs, sources told The Athletic Tuesday ( Getty )

“Karl Ravech has no seat at @espn while blowhard @stephenasmith makes millions upon millions of dollars per year and rarely has any clue what he's talking about. Unbelievable, ESPN,” someone else wrote while another said, “In the bigger picture: class, integrity, respect are all disappearing everywhere.”

Still, Ravech continued his personal podcast with professionalism only hours after learning his fate at ESPN.

On his Dirt From The Dugout podcast Tuesday night, Ravech said, “For many of you that are on here, you’re members and soon-to-be (guest) Adam Wainwright, there’s a lot going on with ESPN, we’re well aware of it, we’re not going to discuss that tonight.

“This is all about the parents’ dugout, it’s all about Dirt From The Dugout, it’s all about trying to help parents, which ultimately here is our goal and young players on their journeys.”

Ravech has not spoken out further about the ESPN news.

Many of the cuts are reportedly connected to ESPN’s integration with NFL Network, including the expected departure of NFL insider Tom Pelissero, one of the network’s top reporters, according to the outlet.

A memo from ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro to employees Tuesday morning, obtained by The Independent, did not identify those impacted by the layoffs but said the cuts followed a review of the company’s teams, resources and structure after integrating acquired NFL assets.

ESPN acquired NFL Network in late January as part of a deal with the league that also gave the NFL a 10 percent stake in ESPN.

ESPN declined to provide further comment.

The UK has experienced record-breaking temperatures this summer, with three consecutive heatwaves and a severe dry spell turning the nation’s green landscape brown and dry.

Last month was England’s hottest June on record, the Met Office has confirmed, hitting 37.7C in Lingwood, Norfolk on the 26th. This surpassed the 35.6C set in 1957 and equalled the 1976 record.

Sweltering temperatures have continued into July, with 2026 marking the first time that temperatures have reached 35C in May, June and July in the same year.

Many parts of England are now at risk of drought due to prolonged hot and dry conditions, with land and rivers drying up across southern and eastern England.

Satellite images reveal the impact these conditions have had on the natural environment, with extensive browning of green spaces and farmland due to high evaporation and low rainfall.

Only 13 per cent of rivers are currently at normal levels for this time of year, the National Drought Group said.

Many areas have had no rain at all these months. But a spike in demand for water has been met with hosepipe bans now affected over 20 million customers.

Experts have warned that the extreme heats evidence the impacts of human-influenced climate change.

Mike Kendon, a Met Office climate information scientist, said last week: “What we used to think of as extreme, we increasingly consider as normal.

“Every year is adding to the body of evidence showing climate change in the UK,” he added.

“We are right now living in a time of historic and unprecedented change and in terms of temperature, on annual, seasonal, monthly and daily timescales, this evidence shows the climate of the 20th century has now gone.”

A new Met Office report adds that the last four years are all in the top five warmest years in UK history, with 2025 being the hottest. It is possible that 2026 could break the record again.

Alongside the daytime peaks, prolonged ‘tropical nights’ – where temperatures remain above 20C – have caused many to lose sleep and prevented green spaces from fully recovering.

The UK saw a new record for overnight temperatures, with 23.5C recorded at Cardiff Bute Park on 25 June, surpassing the previous record of 20C set in 2023.

Outside of the UK, severe heatwave conditions have been experienced across Europe this year, with France particularly affected by dangerous conditions.

The country recorded over 2,000 excess deaths in June, hitting its hottest ever nationwide temperature on June 24, when it reached nearly 41C in Paris.

Meteorologists say the heatwaves have been caused by a persistent high-pressure ‘heat dome’ over western Europe, which has trapped warm air from the Atlantic and southern regions.

Temperatures now appear to be cooling for most parts of the UK, with the third heatwave of the year ending for much of the country.

However, ITV’s weather service has predicted that another heatwave could begin at the start of August if an area of high pressure that has been detected continues to build.

Torrential rains caused flash floods that inundated homes and businesses, washed out bridges and led to numerous water rescues in portions of West Virginia, authorities said.

Gov. Patrick Morrisey sent 100 National Guard members to the hardest-hit areas in the northern part of the state, and declared a state of emergency for all 55 counties Tuesday night. An additional 200 National Guard members were expected to arrive by late Wednesday morning.

“State and local agencies will remain on the ground for as long as it takes to help affected communities,” Morrisey said in a statement.

Forecasters said up to 7 inches (18 centimeters) of rain fell in some places. No deaths were immediately reported.

The National Weather Service in Charleston warned of life-threatening flooding conditions in some communities Tuesday night, telling people to “SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!”

Bob Pfister said the power remained on at the hotel where he was staying in Weston, even though the first floor was inundated, and most people planned to stay put until Wednesday morning.

“Right now this option is much better than a shelter and a life boat,” Pfister said in a post on Facebook. “If the power goes out that may change a whole lot!”

Video and photos posted to social media showed submerged vehicles in parking lots, including at a Walmart in Weston where muddy water surged far into the store.

Emergency crews reported dozens of rescues of people stuck in submerged vehicles. However, some rescuers were unable to get to locations where floodwaters had cut off access.

Flash flood warnings in the state expired by Wednesday morning. Other warnings were issued for parts of neighboring Virginia.

The heavy rains were part of wide-ranging storms that also produced reports of tornadoes stretching from the Cincinnati area across New Jersey to the New York City suburbs. Damage from a possible tornado was reported in the area of St. Marys and Belmont in West Virginia.

Emergency service communication channels were buzzing with activity late Tuesday night in Lewis and Upshur counties, which have about 40,000 residents combined.

First responders were performing water rescues for hours Tuesday night into Wednesday, Lewis County Commissioner Agnes Quinn Queen said.

“The devastation across our county is extensive,” she said in a social media post.

A sinkhole caused by the storm swallowed a vehicle at a bar Tuesday night in Fayetteville, in southern West Virginia.

Morrisey urged residents to stay at home and said travel conditions remained hazardous Tuesday night. Floodwaters forced the closure of portions of Interstate 79, U.S. Route 48 and numerous secondary roads. The ground was already saturated after storms dumped more than 2 inches (5 centimeters) of rain throughout the state on Saturday.

Tuesday’s storms occurred a decade after 23 people died after heavy rains fell for hours over the same areas.

Data from a U.S. Geological Survey water gauge showed one creek tributary, Sand Run, rose to a record level near Buckhannon, topping the mark set during a November 1985 flood event that resulted in 47 deaths statewide.

___

Associated Press writer Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut, contributed to this report.

News.title: Grandchildren of Thomas the Tank Engine author in HMRC court fight over huge tax bill on royalties
News.content:

The grandchildren of Thomas the Tank Engine's creator have been spared a potentially massive tax bill on their share of the multimillion-pound royalties generated by their grandad's "really useful engine", after HMRC lost a crucial High Court test case last week.

First published in 1945 after being invented by Rev Wilbert Awdry to entertain his sick two-year-old son Christopher, the popular children's books have spawned an industry encompassing TV, films, toys and theme parks which was reportedly generating an annual turnover of $1bn by 2011 and a profit of over £35m a year.

Rev Awdry and wife Margaret had three children, Christopher, Veronica and Hilary, with the trio giving him seven grandchildren.

But almost 30 years after the author's death, the managers of a trust fund he left for the benefit of his grandkids ended up fighting HMRC in court in a bid to pay out less tax on the royalties created by the much-loved steam train.

Mr Justice Richards at London's High Court last week found against arguments put forward by HMRC lawyers that the royalty payments ought to count as income for trust law purposes and therefore be liable for potential income tax payments of up to 45%.

Wilbert Vere Awdry OBE was an English Anglican clergyman, railway enthusiast and children's author. He was best known for creating Thomas the Tank Engine in his books, The Railway Series, writing the first 26 books between 1945 to 1972.

The books have since spawned an industry encompassing TV, films, toys and theme parks which was reportedly generating an annual turnover of $1bn by 2011 and a profit of over £35m a year.

open image in gallery Hilary Fortnum and Veronica Chambers, two of Reverend Awdry’s children, with Thomas The Tank Engine ( Supplied by Champion News )

That was the year that the rights in the brand were acquired by US toy giants Mattel - owners of Barbie, Hotwheels and Masters of the Universe - when they bought HiT Entertainment for $680m (£426m).

HiT by that time owned the rights to Thomas alongside other kids' characters, including Barney the purple dinosaur, Fireman Sam and Angelina Ballerina, with Thomas branded products alone generating profit of over £35m a year.

The copyright to the Rev Awdry's books was signed away by him to his then publishers in 1985 - shortly after Thomas made his first TV appearance - in return for a deal guaranteeing him a share of any future royalties.

Half of those royalties were tied up in a trust fund for the benefit of the clergyman's grandchildren in 1987 at which time his grandkids - Christopher's son and daughter Richard and Verity, Veronica's kids Mark and Claire, and Hilary's three children Sara, Simon and Rachel - ranged in age between six and 17.

All are now adults, but almost 30 years after the author's death the trust fund's managers ended up in a court fight with HMRC in a bid to pay less tax on the money churned out by Thomas.

Setting out the shape of the case in his judgment, Mr Justice Richards said: "On 16 October 1985, Reverend Awdry entered into a deed of assignment with his then publishers.

"Reverend Awdry assigned, to the extent that they had not already been assigned to the publishers or their predecessors in title, the entire copyright throughout the world in certain defined 'Works' and 'Illustrations' together with such rights as may subsist in what was described as the 'Railway Format'.

"In return, the publishers were to pay Reverend Awdry a stream of royalties...during the term of the copyrights so assigned.

"On 10 March 1987, Reverend Awdry made the settlement...to transfer to the trustees the property and assets set out in the schedule.

"The settlement recorded that Reverend Awdry wished to make provision for his grandchildren, who were individually named and described as the 'beneficiaries' in the settlement.

"The schedule described the property and assets referred to as: one half of all royalties paid to the settlor after the date of this deed.

"The trustees are party to this claim as claimants because they wish to know how the settlement should be administered.

"HMRC is party to the claim because they have an interest in the outcome as they are likely to be entitled to more tax if the royalties are categorised as income for trust law purposes."

open image in gallery The Awdry family ( Supplied by Champion News )

Going on to find against the taxman and sparing the reverend's grandkids trust fund a potentially massive tax bill, the judge said that the royalties were themselves the assets and capital of the trust, rather than counting legally as income generated.

"The royalties received by the settlement are most naturally analysed as 'fruit' of the copyrights in the Railway Series. Those copyrights are not assets of the settlement...the royalties are the capital of the settlement.

"The defendants argue that this is the wrong way of looking at matters. They submit that the royalties received by the settlement are fruit of the right to receive those royalties, which is an asset of the settlement.

"I acknowledge that this is an alternative way of looking at matters. However, I am not satisfied that trust law principles require the matter to be viewed in that way.

"Overall, I regard it as much more realistic to regard the royalties as fruit of the copyright in the Railway Series rather than as fruit of a right to receive payment.

"Overall, I see nothing to override the intention plainly expressed in the settlement itself. I consider that the royalties received by the trustees are capital for trust law purposes."

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: ‘Cole Palmer out here playing super agent’ say fans as Morgan Rogers reveals what mate did ahead of Chelsea transfer
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans believe Cole Palmer has been masquerading as a super agent this summer.

New signing Morgan Rogers has revealed how his old pal has been in touch “non-stop”.



Rogers, 23, has joined the Blues from Aston Villa for a British record transfer fee of £117million.

And his move to Stamford Bridge means he will link up with former Manchester City Academy team-mate Palmer.



Rogers, who has laid down the claim to being the creator of Palmer’s ‘ice cold’ celebration, has revealed how the 24-year-old helped to convince him to join Chelsea.

Speaking in the club’s announcement, the England World Cup star said: “I’ve known Cole since I was about 14, first in the England [youth] teams and then when we were both at Man City together.

“We’ve been speaking about this for a while; we always would love to have played together.

“So, for it to happen, we’re both excited. He’s non-stop ringing my phone, texting me, and I can’t wait.

“I think that’s probably the most special thing, playing with one of your best friends and being around him every day.

“It’s something I’m really excited about.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fans were loving Palmer’s apparent enthusiasm to reunite with Rogers on the pitch, with one saying: “Cole Palmer out here playing super agent with those non-stop texts. Proper mates reuniting at Chelsea is the kind of story football needs. This is going to be special.”

A second said: “When Palmer starts texting, you know it’s serious.”

A third added: “This will be the best duo in the league.”

Another said: “Agent Cole Palmer completely secured the biggest transfer of the summer.”

Rogers starred in seven games for Thomas Tuchel‘s Three Lions across the World Cup, which saw England manage their best finish since 1966 with third.



Palmer was a controversial omission from Tuchel’s squad, something which became an even more prominent debate when England struggled to break down opponents who played in a low block against them, such as Ghana and DR Congo.

Regardless, the pair will now be reunited for next season’s campaign, hoping to score some silverware as they did with Man City in the 2020 FA Youth Cup final when both got on the scoresheet – ironically in a 3-2 win over Chelsea’s own Cobham Academy starlets.

Liam Delap also played in that game and is one of SIX former City grads – purchased at a combined cost of £300million – expected to turn out for Xabi Alonso’s Blues next season.



Despite their very close relationship, Chelsea did not ask Palmer to get in touch with Rogers and try to sway him towards signing after long-term interest from Arsenal.

Instead, it was new manager Xabi Alonso who led the charm offensive to scupper Gunners’ hopes of landing their priority target this summer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rogers is the second senior signing Chelsea have made so far this summer that wasn’t pre-negotiated after Marco Palestra’s arrival from Atalanta for up to £48m.

Geovany Quenda is another signing arriving this summer, but that deal was negotiated with Sporting Lisbon last year.

Sports.title: Chelsea have spent £300million on ex-Man City kids since 2023… Blues’ famous Cobham core is down to FOUR players
Sports.content:
IT gets to a point where fans are completely lost on Chelsea’s master plan to make it back to the upper echelons of football.

Whether it is tracing every transfer move made by Arsenal or tracking Manchester City’s academy stars, Chelsea are wading through the start of a new era.



Since 2023, Stamford Bridge have splashed out around £300MILLION on ex-City youth.

The latest is Morgan Rogers.



Fresh off the plane from the World Cup, Rogers made headlines as he became Britain’s most expensive player EVER.

The Blues hijacked the £117m move for the Aston Villa star after he was tipped for a move to Premier League champions Arsenal, with the Gunners own valuation not coming close to that outlay.

He is the sixth City academy product to move to west London – the first under Xabi Alonso – in the last three years.

As the 2026/27 season approaches, Alonso’s first-team squad could include TWICE as many City academy graduates than anyone from their own system.

Cole Palmer – another ex-City boy – was sensationally snubbed from Pep Guardiola‘s first-team before forcing a move elsewhere.

Since the 24-year-old made the £40m move to the capital, he has made 131 appearances for Chelsea, scoring 54 times and making 32 assists.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He has even bagged himself an ice empire in the meantime, although he struggled for form last season and did not make Thomas Tuchel‘s England squad for the World Cup.

Back in 2020, Rogers and Palmer both scored for Man City in their 3-2 victory over Chelsea in the FA Youth Cup final.

Liam Delap led the line at St George’s Park that night – and that is where the pattern begins to emerge.

Rogers, Palmer, Delap. That comes to around £190m.



Then with Romeo Lavia, Jamie Gittens, and Tosin Adarabioyo, the City graduate shopping spree has drawn up a bill of around £300m.

That’s more than enough to buy every adult in the UK a pint on a Friday night – with enough left over to buy the pub.

But that is not to say that no current Chelsea players featured in that dreaded youth final six years ago.

Levi Colwill was there.



And in Alonso’s current first-team, academy graduate Reece James will be there, alongside Trevoh Chalobah and Josh Acheampong – although both could yet exit the club this summer.

The two Chelsea’s graduates’ stay could be coming to an end, with Chalobah linked to Cesc Fabregas’ Como in Serie A.

The Blues do not want to sell Acheampong, 20, but he has expressed a desire for more first-team football, which seems unlikely next season.

Chelsea bowed out of the 2025/26 Premier League season in tenth, having seen Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior, and then Calum McFarlane as permanent and temporary head coaches.



While selling graduates is unpopular with fans, clubs are drawn to it because the fees can be recorded as pure profit under Premier League and Uefa spending rules.

Blues winger Tyrique George made the move to Everton in a deal worth up to £24m, having come up through the academy.

Under Roman Abramovich‘s ownership is was a popular model, with dozens of players – Marc Guehi, Tino Livramento and Tammy Abraham among them – all made way to fund star signings.

Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital’s spending since 2022 has brought a wealth of difficulties as they attempt to balance major spending on new signings.



But in the wide world of football, it seems as though the Premier League can still be a conveyor belt of players, managers, and employees.

Joe Shields – former employee in City’s academy recruitment department – dived into work alongside youth and senior recruitment at Stamford Bridge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tom Glick went from chief commercial and operating officer at City to Chelsea’s president of business. And recently, Enzo Maresca went from assistant manager at City to Chelsea’s head coach, before returning to City to replace Pep Guardiola.

There is also the missed opportunity of former City academy player Michael Olise who made the move to Bayern Munich in spite of Chelsea’s interest – as well as Nico O’Reilly.

Sports.title: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert facing ban as he’s slapped with three new charges over Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON boss Tonda Eckert has been slapped with three charges over the “Spygate” scandal.

Saints were sensationally thrown out of last season’s Championship play-offs by the EFL after admitting multiple counts of spying on rivals throughout the campaign.



Middlesbrough replaced them in the play-off final, despite having lost their semi days earlier, but were beaten by Hull at Wembley.

Saints opted to stick with boss Eckert despite the controversy.



The German could now face a ban himself, after being accused of breaching FA rule Rule E3.1. against Oxford, Middlesbrough and Ipswich.

This rule states that: “A Participant shall at all times act in the best interests of the game and shall not act in any manner which is improper or brings the game into disrepute or use any one, or a combination of, violent conduct, serious foul play, threatening, abusive, indecent or insulting words or behaviour.”



An FA statement read: “Southampton FC’s Tonda Eckert has been charged with three breaches of FA rule E3.1 in relation to misconduct between December 2025 and May 2026.

“It’s alleged that the head coach acted in an improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute by directing and/or authorising the observation of training sessions of Oxford United FC, Ipswich Town FC and Middlesbrough FC ahead of fixtures between these clubs and Southampton FC in December 2025, April 2026 and May 2026 respectively.

“Tonda Eckert has until Tuesday 28 July 2026 to provide his responses.”

In a statement of their own, Southampton subsequently acknowledged the charges, while vowing to “cooperate fully and openly with The FA”.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

They then added: “Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026/27 Championship season.

“The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.”

Saints have already been charged as a club by the EFL for watching Oxford, Boro and Ipswich training sessions.

In addition to being expelled from the play-offs, Southampton are also set to start the new season on minus-four points.



Addressing the controversy, Eckert told BBC radio last week: “It hurts for a number of different reasons.

“It’s tough to read some of the things that are out there, I’ve held my hand up for this judgement on something I have authorised.

“I am responsible and I apologise for bad judgement; we’ve been in now for a week and there comes a point to look forward and from the first day back in, there’s been lots of smiles and a good energy in the place again.”

Former Canada women’s coach Bev Priestman received a one-year ban from Fifa following a spying scandal around the 2024 Olympics, before eventually returning to work with New Zealand side Wellington Phoenix.

Eckert replaced Will Still as Southampton boss last September and has won 21 of his 35 games in charge to date.



Among these triumphs was a memorable FA Cup victory over Arsenal at St Mary’s.

Saints will begin their new campaign with an EFL Cup trip to Colchester on August 8.

Eight days later they will kick off their Championship campaign by travelling to Watford.

Sports.title: Phil Foden comments on Enzo Maresca speak volumes as he signs new Man City contract
Sports.content:
Phil Foden admits he is relishing working under new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca - after signing a new and improved deal at the Etihad.

Foden has put his World Cup heartbreak behind by penning a contract that will keep him at the club until 2030. The 26-year-old is one of the most decorated players in the club's history, having won a staggering 20 major trophies.

And he is targeting even more under former first team coach Maresca, who has returned to replace the great Pep Guardiola in the blue half of Manchester.

Foden, who was left out of the England squad for the World Cup, said: "Committing my future to City means everything to me. Playing for this Club is all I've ever wanted to do and it’s always an honour to wear the shirt. It's not lost on me that I’ve been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won.

‌



"But we're always looking to the future and trying to win more.

Sports.title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert charged by FA over Spygate saga and could face ban
Sports.content:
Southampton boss Tonda Eckert charged by FA over Spygate saga and could face ban

Southampton were booted out of the Championship play-offs after being caught spying on opponents and their head coach Tonda Eckert is still in hot water with the FA

View 2 Images Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA (Image: Rich Linley - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Tonda Eckert has been charged with misconduct by the Football Association over the 'Spygate' scandal which rocked the Championship play-offs last season.

‌



Southampton were expelled from the play-offs back in May despite beating Middlesbrough over two legs after a staff member was caught spying on an opponents' training sessions.

‌



The Saints were also given a four-point penalty for the 2026-27 campaign, with Middlesbrough being subsequently reinstated for the play-off final, which was won 1-0 by Hull City at Wembley.

‌



Eckert's position was heavily scrutinised following the fallout from the scandal, with an investigation subsequently being launched into the 33-year-old.

It has now been confirmed that Eckert has been charged with three counts of bringing the game into disrepute after spying was authorised against Middlesbrough, Ipswich Town and Oxford United, leaving his future up in the air.

An FA statement confirming the news on Wednesday read: “It’s alleged that the head coach acted in an improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute by directing and/or authorising the observation of training sessions of Oxford United FC, Ipswich Town FC and Middlesbrough FC ahead of fixtures between these clubs and Southampton FC in December 2025, April 2026 and May 2026 respectively.”

‌



It remains to be seen what punishment Eckert will be handed, with previous reports indicating that the German could be hit with a ban by the FA. They have the power to punish individuals, with the EFL only able to impose sanctions on clubs.

View 2 Images Southampton were booted out of the play-offs despite beating Middlesbrough over two legs (Image: Robin Jones, Getty Images)

Southampton confirmed that they and Eckert acknowledged the charges in a statement of their own, adding: "Tonda and the club will continue to co-operate fully and openly with the FA.

‌



"Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 Championship season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.

"We are unable to comment further while the process remains ongoing, but we will provide an update to supporters as soon as we are in a position to do so."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has agreed to pledge his future to Manchester United. And the Portuguese superstar is expected to confirm he is staying at Old Trafford before the end of this month.

Fernandes is currently on his summer break, following his participation in the World Cup in North America. The United captain is due back to pre-season training next week.

Talks between his representatives and United bosses about a new and improved deal have been on-going. And while no agreement has been reached, it's understood Fernandes has decided to commit himself to United.

His future had been in doubt for the last 12 months.

‌



Last summer, Fernandes considered leaving United to cash-in on a lucrative deal in the Saudi Pro League. He decided to have one more season at Old Trafford instead, to see if the club could match his ambitions.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane's France nightmare as fractured squad split after Kylian Mbappe's actions
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane's France nightmare as fractured squad split after Kylian Mbappe's actions

Zinedine Zidane is rumoured to be taking over from Didier Deschamps as the manager of the French national side

View 3 Images Kylian Mbappe will work under Zinedine Zidane for France (Image: Getty)

Zinedine Zidane is widely expected to become the next manager of the French national team. And he could be walking into a deeply fractured environment, with Kylian Mbappe at the heart of tensions.

‌



According to French outlet L'Équipe, the Real Madrid icon will officially take over on September 1, replacing Didier Deschamps, who announced he would step down at the end of this summer's World Cup.

‌



The French Football Federation (FFF) has yet to confirm the appointment. However, president Philippe Diallo has said an announcement will be made before the end of the month and Le Parisien reports that Zidane has already begun assembling his coaching staff.

‌



Yet the nation's star man, Mbappe, could be a source of friction for Zidane after a series of controversies emerged following France's unsuccessful World Cup campaign, which ended in fourth place. Mirror Football takes a look at Mbappe and his current relationship with his national team.

Kylian Mbappe at the heart of French tensions

Mbappe was allegedly at the centre of escalating friction between the French national squad and the FFF in the lead-up to the World Cup.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Donald Trump backs Gianni Infantino for shocking new job after FIFA World Cup backlash READ MORE :

Can Argentina Premier League players have visas revoked after World Cup uproar? READ MORE :

In the wake of their third-place play-off defeat by England, Deschamps alluded to drama while explaining his choice to resign. “I dictated my exit because it was my choice to make,” he said.

“I resolved that it needed to finish here. And if I took this step, I mean it genuinely, it was not for my own sake. It was for the benefit of the French national squad. I haven't mentioned this until today, but I will speak truthfully, I did not make this choice for myself.

“Because the environment had become completely intolerable, overly fixated on me, just on me. The French team does not merit that.”

‌



Media outlets in France have highlighted a widening divide between the players and the FFF, notably following Diallo's takeover as president. According to RMC, Deschamps perceived a lack of backing from the governing body after the leadership shift, with Zidane now poised to take the helm.

View 3 Images Kylian Mbappe is said to have been involved in some disagreements between the FFF and the France squad. (Image: Eduardo Carmim/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Furthermore, it is claimed that there were ‘a few heated exchanges’ between the manager and the FFF’s deputy director, Erwan Le Prevost. Sticking points reportedly included travel arrangements, family match tickets, and player compensation.

‌



Mbappe was supposedly a key figure in negotiations regarding World Cup bonuses. L'Équipe notes that the players were informed right before flying out that financial rewards would be paid only if they reached the semi-finals, though the Real Madrid forward ultimately secured his preferred outcome.

Highlighting his significant sway, the France captain reportedly also had a hand in persuading the federation to set up a cryotherapy chamber at their base camp.

Mbappe questions World Cup tactics

The French impressed with their performances in the early rounds at the World Cup but were soundly beaten by eventual champions Spain, 2-0, in the semi-finals.

‌



After, Mbappe appeared to question Didier Deschamps' tactical approach. "We were three against two in midfield and against Spain, that's hard. Fabian [Ruiz] and Rodri had plenty of time to play," Mbappe said.

"There was a lack of communication on the press. I think we should have done man-to-man press and force them to run with us.

View 3 Images Didier Deschamps has taken charge of his final France game. (Image: Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



"We didn't play the game we wanted, technically, tactically. When you don't do what you have to do in a World Cup semi-final, you don't win. Spain respected their game plan and what the team usually does. They like to control the ball and the tempo. Our plan was to press them high so they could not install their rhythm.

"We didn't manage to do it. We were too sloppy technically. We could not hurt them when we could have. Even when we recovered the ball, our first touches were not good enough. It is a huge disappointment. But if we are objective, we didn't put all the ingredients to go to the final."

Should Zidane take charge as expected, his first games will come in the Nations League when France take on Turkey, Belgium and Italy in September and early October.

Sports.title: 'I was banned after the World Cup final – but I had no regrets about my behaviour'
Sports.content:
'I was banned after the World Cup final – but I had no regrets about my behaviour'

Leandro Paredes awaits word of any further punishment from the chaos that followed Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain, though he isn't the first to cop a ban on football's biggest stage

View 2 Images Zinedine Zidane is one of the few players who can say they were sent off in a World Cup final (Image: JOHN MACDOUGALL/AFP via Getty Images)

Argentina enforcer Leandro Paredes could be eyeing a lengthy ban for his actions following the World Cup final defeat to Spain. However, he wouldn't be the first to taint the sport's biggest fixture by being sent off in the championship game.

‌



Chaos engulfed the New York-New Jersey Stadium on Sunday when certain members of Lionel Scaloni's squad sparked a brawl with Spain after the full-time whistle. Paredes was the worst offender of all and was shown a post-game red after he grabbed Eric Garcia's throat and flung Gavi to the floor.

‌



The scenes unfolded a full 20 years after Zinedine Zidane's infamous extra-time headbutt on Marco Materazzi. The only two scorers in the 2006 World Cup final in Berlin collided when France's talisman nutted his Italian counterpart in the chest in the 110th minute.

‌



Italy went on to lift the title after winning on penalties, though Zidane explained he felt compelled to respond in light of some despicable comments from Materazzi: "They were things that are very serious. The words were very personal and they concerned my mother and my sister...

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"They were very hard words. You hear them once and you feel bad. You hear it twice. Then you hear it a third time...I'm a man, and I'm telling you that I would rather have been punched in the face than have heard those words. But I heard them and I reacted."

‌



Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Lamine Yamal trolls Argentina's Leandro Paredes during Spain victory parade READ MORE :

Zidane took full ownership of his actions and profusely apologised for reacting as he did. He specifically referenced the "millions of kids" watching from home and their teachers, saying he was wrong to put them in a position where the actions of a national hero have to be explained.

The Real Madrid icon, who received a three-game ban for his actions but retired anyway, was later quizzed about whether he regretted his attack but stood firm: "I can't regret it, because that would mean he was right to have said what he did."

View 2 Images Zidane has said he harbours no regrets for his headbutt on Marco Materazzi (Image: DESK/AFP/Getty Images)

‌



Zidane has since walked back part of his account and told L'Equipe there was no mention of his mother by Materazzi. And the Italian appears to have corroborated the stories after opening up to Italian Football TV in 2023 about what was really said 17 years prior.

"You know the NBA? Trashtalking? My trashtalking was nothing," said the former Inter Milan star. "He offered me his shirt [at the end of the game]. I said ‘no, I’d prefer your sister.'”

As far as we know from the outside, Spain said nothing on par with that to warrant Argentina's post-match attacks in New Jersey. Paredes became physical with multiple players but at no point looked to appeal to the officials for justice over any apparent comments.

‌

Instead, it appears the pain of defeat was the lone driving factor behind the Argentinian assault. And that only came after the South Americans put on a thuggish display for 120 minutes, with Enzo Fernandez also sent off at the end of normal time.

This was in addition to the hot water Argentina already found themselves in for their Falklands banner protest after beating England in the semis. So while Zidane may have stuck out among France's 2006 team for his ban, Argentina appear set to incur FIFA's wrath on a much more widespread scale.

Sports.title: Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design
Sports.content:
Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design

Manchester United have launched their new blue away kit for the 2026/27 season

View 2 Images The new Manchester United away kit

Manchester United will wear blue next season as their new away strip for 2026/27 has been unveiled, returning to a classic look.

Four-time chart-topping rapper Stormzy debuted the kit during the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina as the United fan sported the new blue shirt on his Instagram story.

New signings Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow will line up in the blue strip with the Red Devils well into a busy summer schedule. After a few turbulent years, Michael Carrick has his sights on sparking a fightback to take United back to England and Europe's top table.

The fresh adidas shirt is now available through retailers including Fanatics, with United describing it as a design that "revisits one of the club's most iconic away identities."

United have a long history of sporting a bold blue away kit, though this marks their first return to that distinctive style since the 2016/17 season under José Mourinho - a look that was a regular fixture throughout the 1980s.

The kit features the classic adidas trefoil logo rather than the performance logo found on the home shirt, complemented by a red and white trim.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It is available now through retailers including Fanatics, Kitbag, and the Man United Store, with prices starting at £40 for children and £85 for adults.

In announcing the new away kit, a United statement read: "Manchester United and adidas have unveiled the new away jersey for the 2026/27 season, in a design that revisits one of the club's most iconic away identities through a modern lens.

"Featuring the adidas Trefoil logo, the jersey combines elite performance innovation with a strong connection to football culture, celebrating a look that has long resonated on and off the pitch.

"Built on a bold royal blue base, the jersey brings together familiar foundations with refined textures and subtle accents, delivering a design that retains the clarity and confidence long associated with Manchester United on the road.

"A central element of the jersey is the engineered tonal stripe running throughout the fabric, adding depth and movement to the design.

"Red and white detailing frames the look across the V-neck collar and sleeve cuffs, creating a sharp contrast against the deep blue base.

"The adidas three stripes sit prominently on the shoulders in red, adding a striking athletic edge, while the club crest sits over the heart, paired with the adidas Trefoil logo, balancing tradition with contemporary design cues.

"Designed for elite performance, the jersey features lightweight, body-mapped 3D engineered fabrics that enhance fit and freedom of movement."

View 2 Images A close-up view of the new Man United away shirt.

Manchester United supporters flocked to social media to share their initial reactions to the 2026/27 away strip. One fan posted on X: "Absolutely beautiful away jersey, a beautiful summery blue, love it."

Another wrote: "What a beautiful away jersey. Manchester United have the best kit in the Premier League."

Article continues below

Not everybody was won over, however, with one commenter stating: "Not that great unlike the 2020/2021 season."

Another supporter declared: "Finally an away kit that doesn't look like a training bib. This one's winning trophies in 26/27, mark my words."

Sports.title: Southampton boss Eckert charged by FA over Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA with misconduct and potentially bringing the game into disrepute over the 'Spygate' scandal.

The EFL expelled Southampton from the Championship play-offs in May and handed the club a four-point deduction for the 2026/27 season after they admitted "multiple breaches" relating to the unauthorised filming of their opponents' training, including before their semi-final against Middlesbrough.

Southampton beat Middlesbrough and were due to play Hull City in the play-off final before Boro were reinstated. Southampton appealed the decision, but the punishments were upheld by a League Arbitration Panel.

During the Spygate hearing, the EFL only had the power to charge clubs, not individuals. The FA waited for the EFL process to run its course before launching its own investigation.

The FA has now charged Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1, during the period between December 2025 and May 2026, by "directing and/or observing" training sessions of Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough ahead of fixtures against those clubs.

Rule E3.1 states: "A participant shall at all times act in the best interests of the game and not act in any manner which is improper or brings the game into disrepute or use any one, or a combination of violent conduct, serious foul play, threatening, abusive, indecent or insulting words or behaviour".

In response, Southampton say they remain "fully supportive" of Eckert and will "continue to cooperate fully and openly with The FA".

Eckert has until Tuesday July 28 to provide his responses.

Eckert 'loved' spying information

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton boss Tonda Eckert 'loved' the information gathered by a junior analyst intern when spying on one of his team's opponents, according to newly released messages.

In June, Eckert said he took full responsibility "for everything that happened", apologising to players, staff and supporters.

At that time, Southampton chairman Dragan Solak admitted Eckert had made a "mistake" but said the club was "fully behind him", reaffirming their target of winning promotion to the Premier League.

In the written reasons released following the League Arbitration Panel's decision to dismiss Southampton's appeal against their punishment, Saints' conduct was described as a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

Eckert "loved" the information a junior analyst intern gathered when spying on one of his team's opponents, according to messages used as evidence in the hearing.

The written reasons detail how analysts felt pressure to carry out jobs asked of them as a colleague had lost their job earlier in the season.

The panel added: "A reprimand is considered appropriate because of the way in which junior members of staff were put under pressure to carry out activities which they felt were, at the least, morally wrong."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports' Mark McAdam, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert reveals the challenges he has faced after the Spygate scandal that resulted in their expulsion from the Championship play-offs.

Eckert told Sky Sports News last week that he had received police protection amid threats during the Spygate scandal.

"It's been an emotional summer. I can't lie, obviously, when the news broke towards the back end of last season, it's tough. It's not easy in that very moment. It's not easy to look into the eyes of the players. They're just so disappointed, and so many emotions coming out.

"You get so many threats at one point. You have police protection at one point; you can't drive a car. It's tough to deal with that for the very moment.

"When things calmed down with time, and I went back home, different challenges at home, you have a moment to reflect. I think that over the months there's also been a lot of positives that we can take into next season.

"After a couple of weeks, that excitement comes back in to go again and show what we are about. That's been the feeling since coming back into the training ground. We are in the second week of pre-season now. Players have come back in very good shape, with a smile on their face and ready to go again."

Spygate timeline: How did we get here?

May 7: Middlesbrough make formal complaint to the EFL alleging a Southampton member of staff spied on their training session three days before their Championship play-off semi-final first leg.

May 9: Boro boss Kim Hellberg accuses Southampton of cheating after the first leg ends in a 0-0 draw at the Riverside Stadium.

May 12: Southampton charged with a breach of EFL regulations in relation to the spying accusations. Southampton request additional time to conduct an internal review.

The play-off semi-final second leg is played at St Mary's. Shea Charles' extra-time winner earns Southampton a 2-1 victory and a place in the Championship play-off final.

Emotional Hellberg hits out at "disgraceful spying", before Saints boss Tonda Eckert storms out of his press conference after being asked: "Are you a cheat?"

May 13: Photos allegedly showing the Southampton analyst near Middlesbrough's training ground released publicly.

May 14: It is announced the independent hearing to determine Southampton's fate will take place on or before Tuesday May 19. In a statement, the EFL say "the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture."

May 15: Middlesbrough publicly call for Southampton's expulsion from the play-offs. In a statement, they said: "In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final."

May 18: Middlesbrough players return to training as the outcome of the independent disciplinary hearing nears.

May 19: EFL announces Southampton expelled from play-off final after hearing.

May 20: Southampton appeal rejected.

May 21: FA confirm they will begin their own investigation into Spygate.

May 23: Middlesbrough lose 1-0 to Hull City in the Championship play-off final.

June 2: Eckert takes full responsibility for Spygate as Southampton owner Dragan Solak backs head coach.

June 17: Eckert tells Sky Sports News he received police protection amid threats during Spygate.

July 22: FA charges Southampton head coach Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1.

Sports.title: Lingfield and Worcester host competitive Wednesday cards
Sports.content:
Worcester and Lingfield are the venues for today's racing, with National Hunt and Flat action on the agenda.

8.10 Lingfield - Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest trappy affair

Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest a trappy-looking Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap at Lingfield.

Top weight Hilltop is a consistent performer who ran another solid race when third over this course and distance in May and should give another bold bid off the same mark.

George Boughey's Kaori is a lightly raced type who is yet to win in five starts. She wasn't beaten far when third at Yarmouth and drops back to seven furlongs with the hope of more to offer under Billy Loughnane.

Mojito ran out an impressive winner on her penultimate run at Doncaster before disappointing when favourite at Salisbury and has a bit to prove here.

2.25 Worcester - Red-hot Regal Renaissance seeks a four-timer

Regal Renaissance seeks a fourth success on the bounce as she takes on eight rivals in this Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase at Worcester.

Jack Jones' in-form mare landed her final start for trainer Henry Daly in May and has two wins from two starts for her new connections. She stayed on strongly when outpointing Fringill Dike at Market Rasen and this looks a good opportunity to follow up despite a 2lb rise.

Harry Hope looks a danger for the Ben Pauling and Jones combination. He has an excellent strike-rate over fences and should strip fitter for his last outing at Stratford.

Axel Bleue scored over this track and trip 21 days ago and remains unexposed over fences.

4.00 Worcester - Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash

Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash in a competitive Dolphin Tec Handicap Hurdle at 4pm.

Media Mogul recorded a first hurdling success when challenging late over this course and distance last month and makes appeal as he heads into handicaps off a mark 105.

Playful Fox represents the powerful Skelton team and is another who arrives on the back of a victory at Stratford. That was his debut win over hurdles, and he looks well-suited to this two-mile distance.

Others to note include Jamie Snowden's Kernie d'Airy, who got off the mark at the third attempt over jumps here last month and is another who makes his handicap debut. Ez Tiger ran well in second over this course and distance last month and goes again today, with Bryan Carver retaining the ride.

Best of the rest

Back at Lingfield, Emma's Letter will be fancied to give Ed Dunlop and Billy Loughnane a positive start to proceedings in the attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (6.10pm). This three-year-old daughter of Saxon Warrior has only been nudged up 3lbs for success at Nottingham the last day and with only three rivals to beat, she could go in again.

An hour later, Dreamlover represents Richard Spencer and Phil Cunningham in the Follow @attheraces On X Nursery Handicap. Connections will be hoping a return to five furlongs will pay dividends for this gelding, who drops significantly down in class for this assignment. Romidijo found just one too good at Chepstow the last day and could also relish the drop in distance.

The 7.40pm Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Novice Stakes sees the 89-rated Asuka take on Coilltedudeisback and Yazoo. George Boughey's charge is likely to go off a very short price in the colours of the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid.

Watch every race from Worcester and Lingfield, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Sports.title: 'This means everything to me' - Foden signs new Man City contract
Sports.content:
Man City have announced Phil Foden has signed a new contract at the club.

The 26-year-old - whose previous deal was set to expire next summer - has agreed to remain at the Etihad Stadium until 2030.

Speaking in an interview published on the club's official media channels, Foden said: "Committing my future to City means everything to me.

Image: The 26-year-old has won 20 trophies with City

"Playing for this club is all I've ever wanted to do and it's always an honour to wear the shirt.

"It's not lost on me that I've been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won, but we're always looking to the future and trying to win more.

"I can only thank the club, staff, team-mates and fans who continue to put their faith in me and trust that I give everything I can for City and I hope I'll be able to repay you for years to come.

"I can't wait to work with Enzo [Maresca] again. He was brilliant during the Treble season - someone all the players respected and loved working with. To have him back here is exciting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports football journalist Laura Hunter says Enzo Maresca won't be afforded time to excel as Manchester City boss.

"Personally, I know I've improved so much from working with our coaches and world-class squad and as many of the legends who were here when I first broke through move on, I am excited for the next phase of my career at this great club."

Foden has made 369 appearances and scored 110 goals for City's first team since making his debut in a Champions League game against Feyenoord on November 21 2017.

In 2025/26, he played 50 times, scoring 10 goals and providing seven assists.

Alongside John Stones and Bernardo Silva - who both left the Etihad this summer - the academy graduate is the most decorated player in the club's history, having won 20 major trophies, including six Premier League titles, one UEFA Champions League, three FA Cups, five League Cups, one UEFA Super Cup, one FIFA Club World Cup and three Community Shields.
