Sports.title: Inside the incredible rise of Madeleine McCann's brother Sean - who 'HATED' swimming: How 'sport-obsessed' mother Kate, 5am wake ups and surviving 'disgusting' training sessions inspired him to Scotland call up
Sports.content:
When Sean McCann stood behind the blocks of the 50-metre swimming pool at Loughborough University for the very first time, he was an 18-year-old with a dream.

He dreamed to compete for Scotland and Team GB on the senior international stage. And on Saturday, at the age of 21, after years of surviving 'disgusting' training sessions, McCann is on the cusp of realising his life goal.

Almost two decades on from the tragic disappearance of his older sister Madeleine, who was abducted from the family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, the Scot will take to the pool to compete in the 400m freestyle heats at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Sean was in the room when Madeleine's abduction unfolded. The 21-year-old, who was two years old at the time of his family's unimaginable tragedy and does not remember the huge global fallout from the case, has received unconditional support from his parents, Gerry and Kate, on his swimming journey.

They have remained a pillar for Sean during his sporting ventures, with Kate having originally introduced him to swimming which he admitted to 'hating at first', with the youngster not wanting to go to lessons.

The couple regularly attend swimming meets to cheer on their son, who has a twin sister named Amelie, and are said to be 'enthusiastic' about distance swimming.

Madeline McCann's younger brother Sean will swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games

Sean has had an incredible rise through the swimming ranks in Scotland and Great Britain

One source, who wishes to remain anonymous, expressed to Daily Mail Sport that the parents are 'really, really supportive' and 'are always there turning up', despite the potential they could be put in the spotlight after everything they have been through.

Saturday marks a monumental moment in the young man's career, and takes him one step closer to his ultimate goal of competing at the Los Angeles Olympics in two years' time.

His journey to the Commonwealth Games began at the age of eight, when he finally got over his fear of the pool. McCann joined Charnwood Triathlon Club, with the hope of becoming the next Alistair Brownlee rather than Michael Phelps.

It was there he discovered his talent for swimming. Soon enough, he wanted to train in the pool more and more, so he joined Loughborough Town Swimming Club to quench that desire, before eventually being handpicked to move to City of Leicester.

At youth level, McCann was clearly talented. He came seventh in the 17-year-old age group 400m freestyle at the British Summer Championships in 2022, while he represented Scotland at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago just a year later.

But it wasn't until he got to the university that has been on his doorstep his whole life that everything changed.

Loughborough University has one of the most prestigious swimming programs not just in the UK but in the world. It has developed stars such as Adam Peaty, who is arguably the greatest swimmer this country has ever seen, Daniel Wiffen, 800m freestyle reigning Olympic champion, and Liam Tancock, former 50m backstroke world record holder. The program has no shortage of heritage.

And McCann took to it like a duck to water. After initially being plopped in the Performance Development squad, McCann sliced a huge chunk off his 400m freestyle time, taking it from 4:01.67 to 3:56.22 in just one year of training at Loughborough.

This seismic improvement saw him promoted to the High Performance squad with Andi Manley, who coaches Wiffen.

Those who have trained with McCann at Loughborough, and elsewhere, made it clear that this remarkable progress is down to his mentality and drive to succeed.

Team Scotland international swimmer, Charlie Hutchison, tells Daily Mail Sport: ‘He’s a workhorse, just like everybody else in that squad. We do some disgusting training sessions, but he is never one to complain or moan. He just gets on with it.

‘This is definitely something he has worked on when he didn’t have as many people to race against and then moving to such a competitive group. Just not being demoralised and pushing forward.

‘It’s great to have him on the team as part of Team Scotland.’

Sean was inspired to start swimming by his mother Kate, although he admits to hating the sport at first

Sean's older sister Madeline went missing in 2007 when Sean was just two years old

Insiders have explained to Daily Mail Sport how McCann used to have to wake up at 5.15am most mornings to make training, with the perceived 'higher' squads swimming at more favourable times.

But McCann was never one to moan during those times, and put in the 'hard yards' to progress into the next squad and make his dreams come true.

Hutchison continues: 'He’s on the path to do very well. His rise through the Scottish ranks was on the Scottish junior team. He’s gone from strength to strength, dropping almost 12 seconds from when he first joined.’

McCann has now taken his 400m freestyle time down to an impressive 3:50.66, with the seconds just dropping with each passing year. But he is not just a one-trick pony; he has proven to be quite versatile in the art of distance swimming.

The Scot will also be competing in both the 800m and 1500m freestyle at the Commonwealth Games, which is almost like making yourself do a half-marathon, deciding that's not enough, and then doing a marathon straight after.

And if that still wasn't enough, he also has a history with open water racing, the marathon equivalent. This is how Olympian Hector Pardoe, who came sixth in the 10km swimming event at the Paris Olympics, met McCann.

The pair met when McCann was representing the Scotland open water development team at the Mallorca Best Fest event, and Pardoe was asked to drop him a message. They spoke about suit sizes, and the double-Olympian also gave him advice on the physicality of the sport.

In the years since, they became team-mates at Loughborough and even room-mates at the European Open Water Championships in Croatia last year.

Pardoe tells Daily Mail Sport: 'He’s a really, really nice guy. He’s a very good trainer, trains really hard, is polite, and a good swimmer.

'I’ve known him for three or four years now; he joined Loughborough in 2023. He’s got a lot quicker. I’d previously seen him on the results page at Nationals, as well.

'When I would be chatting to the Director of Aquatics GB Open Water about new swimmers coming through, he would mention a guy called Sean.’

The distance swimmer originally hails from Leicester and qualifies to represent Scotland through his father, Gerry.

Sean will be swimming the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the home Games in Glasgow

While McCann is set to complete one dream and don the famous blue hat, which has been worn by many a megastar swimmer before him, for the very first time at a senior level, he is hungry for more.

After this summer has come to an end, McCann has his sights set on representing Great Britain at the next Olympics in LA.

If the Scot wants that dream to become reality, he will have to take off over five seconds from his current 400m freestyle personal best. The Olympic 'A Entry Standard' qualifying time is 3:45.46, while the 'B Entry Standard', which only grants qualification at your country's governing body's discretion, is 3:47.71.

Nevertheless, with McCann no stranger to shaving huge chunks off his best times, there is genuine belief that he has what it takes to reach the pinnacle of the sport.

‘His path to making the Olympics certainly isn’t going to be an easy one,' Hutchison adds. 'He is in an event that was strong, went very weak, and now is very strong again. Now he is having to contend with the likes of Jack McMillan, James Guy, and Tyler Melbourne-Smith.

‘But if he carries on his current trajectory, and he continues in one of the best programs in the world for distance swimming, I have no doubt that he can definitely achieve that.’

McCann will be able to use Saturday's event as a barometer to see how far he is off the very best in Britain. Then it's all steam ahead to LA.

Sports.title: World Cup star Vinicius Jr packs on the PDA with his stunning girlfriend in Rio de Janeiro as he celebrates chin surgery success on lavish vacation
Sports.content:
Fresh off a stunning surgical procedure that altered his face, Brazilian football star Vinicius Junior was seen enjoying time with his girlfriend after an early World Cup exit.

The Real Madrid man was out in the sun at Reserva Beach in Rio de Janeiro with his on-and-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

Cameras captured an intimate moment between the two as Fonseca leaned in and planted a kiss on the footballer.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer.

Fonseca and her man continued to enjoy the sun as they relaxed before what should be a lengthy football season.

The photos emerged just hours after it was revealed that Vinicius underwent a stunning procedure.

Real Madrid and Brazil star Vinicius Junior spent time on the beach with his girlfriend

At one point, his partner, Virginia Fonseca, leaned in and planted a kiss on his lips

The pair enjoyed the sunshine after Brazil's early exit from the World Cup

According to Brazilian news outlet TMC, following Brazil's defeat to Norway in the Round of 16, Vinicius headed straight to a dermatologist in Goiania when he landed back in the country following a short vacation in Europe with Fonseca.

A number of photos of the 26-year-old appearing unrecognizable after the op have gone viral on social media, with fans blown away by his remarkable transformation.

Virginia shared a snap of them at her new gym on Monday, having clearly got back together after breaking up before the World Cup, while one of his friends also posted footage of his new-and-improved side profile as he signed a Real Madrid jersey for a fan.

Vinicius posed alongside Dr. Alessandro Alarcao, who performed the surgery in Goiania, in another picture that has emerged online.

He underwent the procedure, which 'uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour', to add more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it during the World Cup.

And it seems like the Madrid player is happy with his dramatic new look, as he is all smiles in all of the post-op photos that have surfaced.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer

The pair remained close just hours after photos emerged of Vinicius' new look

The Brazil superstar looks completely different after undergoing chin harmonization surgery

'MANNNN WHO THE F*** IS THAT,' a third said in bewilderment.

Sports.title: Wolves forced to CANCEL training as banned star refuses to leave the pitch - and extra security is enforced to keep player away from Compton Park
Sports.content:
Wolves' preparations for life in the Championship descended into farce on Monday when training was cancelled because a player refused to leave the pitch.

Striker Tolu Arokodare stood his ground when new manager Cesar Peixoto told him not to train with the first team.

And Wolves organised extra security at their training ground, Compton Park, to prevent the 25-year-old from entering.

Arokodare, who spent last season with Wolves as they were relegated from the Premier League, faced disciplinary action in April after getting into a physical altercation with team-mate Mateus Mane following their 4-0 thrashing by West Ham.

He will not be part of the squad travelling to Maidenhead for a pre-season friendly this evening. Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

Peixoto, who joined from Portuguese club Gil Vicente in June, has insisted he will be a firm hand with his players.

Wolves cancelled training after striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch - and called for extra security to keep him away

New manager Cesar Peixoto initially left Arokodare out of the team's pre-season training camp

In his first interview, he said: 'Firstly, I'm a very demanding coach.

'But, I believe in giving others maximum freedom and maximum responsibility. I want us to work as a team and as a unit and build a good environment. This is important to me, but I know very well what I want from the team. I want my team to be organised with and without the ball.

'Secondly, I want a team with intensity and to be aggressive and win duels.

'The third one is I want to show the quality of the players. To play an offensive game and to try and press high. To try and be the main character of the games. I want to win games, but I want to win while playing good football. With passion and energy.

'[The supporters can expect] a team with ambition. A strong character and identity and a strong idea of the game. A team that never gives up to win three points and to try and make the fans proud.'

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry. The Nigerian striker scored three Premier League goals last campaign.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Wolves as well as Arokodare's representatives.

Demoting players from the first-team or forcing them to train in isolation is banned under new rules introduced by FIFA in June.

The striker faced disciplinary action after clashing with team-mate Mateus Mane - but the duo shared supportive posts in an attempt to defuse the situation

Arokodare scored three Premier League goals campaign and could be moving to Serie A

FIFA reached an agreement with FIFPRO, the worldwide players' union, to better protect players from what is deemed an 'abusive practice'.

Chelsea's 'bomb squad' and treatment of players such as Raheem Sterling has come under scrutiny in recent seasons.

Clubs could face financial or sporting punishments under the new protections unless there is a genuine sporting reason for the player's exclusion.

Banishing them from first-team training cannot now be used as a tactic just to force them to find another club.

Daily Mail Sport has also contacted FIFA and FIFPRO.

Sports.title: More chaos at Southampton! Spying Saints boss Tonda Eckert hit with fresh charges for THREE breaches by the FA after play-off scandal - as club face nervous wait over new sanctions
Sports.content:
Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA with three breaches of misconduct following the Spygate scandal.

The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-off final back in May after admitting they had spied on rival teams during the 2025-26 season.

That came after a club analyst was spotted filming Middlesbrough's training session ahead of Southampton's play-off semi-final against Boro, triggering a major crisis at the south coast club.

Southampton won that tie 2-1 on aggregate but an independent commission subsequently expelled them from the final and also handed them a four-point deduction for the coming season.

The independent commission found that there was a 'contrived and determined plan from the top down' to embark on a spying operation, with boss Tonda Eckert coming under particular scrutiny.

The FA subsequently launched their own investigation into the saga, with potential ramifications including bans for those involved, most notably boss Eckert and the intern analyst William Salt.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA with three breaches of misconduct following the Spygate scandal

The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-off final in May following the saga

And on Wednesday, the FA released a statement confirming that Eckert had been charged over the spying.

It read: 'Southampton FC's Tonda Eckert has been charged with three breaches of FA Rule E3.1 in relation to misconduct between December 2025 and May 2026.

'It's alleged that the head coach acted in an improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute by directing and/or authorising the observation of training sessions of Oxford United FC, Ipswich Town FC and Middlesbrough FC ahead of fixtures between these clubs and Southampton FC in December 2025, April 2026 and May 2026.

'Tonda Eckert has until Tuesday 28 July 2026 to provide his responses.'

In response, a statement from Southampton read: 'Southampton Football Club and First Team Head Coach Tonda Eckert acknowledge today’s charges from The FA relating to a breach of Rule E3.1.

'Tonda and the club will continue to cooperate fully and openly with The FA. Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 Championship season.

'The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.

'We are unable to comment further while the process remains ongoing, but we will provide an update to supporters as soon as we are in a position to do so.'

The statement released by Southampton was originally posted at around 10am on Wednesday, before the club deleted it, causing confusion among fans. It was then reshared at 11.36am, with the exact same wording.

If found guilty, Eckert could be punished with anything from a heavy fine to a lengthy suspension from football.

But Southampton are understood to believe that, having already been hit with a large sporting sanction by being kicked out of the play-offs, any further action such as a ban for Eckert would be unjust.

A Southampton analyst was caught watching Middlesbrough's training session ahead of the play-off semi final

Eckert and Southampton came under significant scrutiny surrounding the whole incident and were heavily criticised for their poor communication and lack of accountability when the news broke.

Things later intensified when the written reasons for the punishment were released, with several damning revelations about the involvement of Eckert in the spying operation.

Leaked WhatsApp messages revealed the German showing his 'love' of the cheating, with one explaining how Salt was told, ‘You legend. Manager loved it’ after a spying mission on Oxford United in December.

Southampton’s attempts to cover up their cheating were similarly eye-watering.

Despite the pressure, Saints owner Dragan Solak opted to stick with Eckert rather than sack him, with the German coach addressing fans in a video statement in June.

Eckert, speaking in full for the first time since the ruling, hardly blinked in the lengthy video, saying: 'Hi, Saints supporters. What I'm going to say is not going to be perfect, but I will try to be as honest and clear as I can be.

'I think you deserve that. For everything that's happened, I do want to apologise, and I hold my hand up because as a head coach, I am responsible.

'I am responsible for everything that has happened in this football club. I am responsible for everything that has happened in my coaching staff.

'I do apologise to the supporters, to everyone who has travelled with us, who has supported us over so many games.'

In the clip entitled: 'A personal message from Tonda Eckert', he went on: 'To the ones who have shared emotions game by game, who have managed to bring us all the way up to this very end of the season.

'We were supposed to play the biggest game of the season. I apologise to the players, who have done absolutely everything that they can. They have done absolutely everything in the last six months to bring this club back to where it belongs. They would have deserved to play the final.'

He added: 'They would have deserved to play the final with you, just like they've done two years ago, and just like they've done in the semi-final against Man City.

'It hurts to see the employees of the club, it hurts to see the staff, it hurts to see the players who have invested so much in the preparation for games.

'Those who have invested so much to leave their families at home to recover and to prepare for the games coming up, who had hurt so much.

'To see their pain on the day the decision came in, because it has such a big impact, not just on them and their career, but also on their families. I apologise to all of the clubs that have been involved, and mostly I apologise to our supporters.'

Eckert, who could be banned from football, publicly apologised to Saints supporters in June

Southampton owner Dragan Solak threw his backing behind Eckert despite the scandal

Eckert then went on to 'give context' to the spying, arguing that his experiences in different leagues have coloured his thinking.

He explained: 'When I worked in Italy for over four years, every starting line-up that we've chosen for the games was always out in the media before games.

'The reason is that our training sessions, especially the ones before games, have always been observed by the media and have always been observed by opponent teams that we came up against.

'[Pep] Guardiola has spoken about this at his time at Bayern Munich, that it has been common practice in Germany to observe training sessions, knowing that other teams would do the same.

'I don't want to say this to excuse anything that we have done. I just want to give you context in the way that I grew up in the football world.

'There are different rules in England. There are different rules from the EFL. And I should have known them.'

He later added: 'I am a young coach. I have made a mistake, and I take full responsibility. I want to thank Dragan and the board for the support, especially in times like this.

'With everything that I have said, without script and without a predefined statement. Speaking to you from the heart, I hope that you have an overview of what has happened over the last weeks.

'I hope that over time you can understand and forgive, and I hope to see you all soon.'

Sports.title: Inside Katie Boulter and Alex De Minaur's wedding: Laura Robson shares fresh pictures from tennis power couple's 'intimate' nuptials
Sports.content:
Laura Robson has given fans another peek into the wedding of Alex De Minaur and Katie Boulter.

The British tennis star was one of Boulter's bridesmaids as the pair tied the knot at an 'intimate family' ceremony.

The couple got married on the day of the Wimbledon final in a Leicestershire village near where Katie grew up and her parents still live.

According to reports by this publication, locals who had heard about the nuptials were sworn to secrecy, though a few hovered around the church hoping to catch a glimpse of the pair.

Locals had also been banned from taking any photos around the wedding.

While locals may have had some photos for their private collection of the pair tying the knot, it seems any public posting of photo ban that may have been in place, has now been lifted.

Laura Robson shared photos from Katie Boulter and Alex De Minaur's wedding

Boulter stunned in a white gown as she prepared to tie the knot with De Minaur

Robson also shared a photo of De Minaur and Bolton looking full of joy at the altar

Robson was a bridesmaid along with fellow British tennis player Jodie Burrage (second from left)

Robson stunned in a green floor length dress

Robson shared a set of photos on Instagram taking followers behind the curtain, there were selfies with Boulter as well as fellow bridesmaid and British tennis player Jodie Burrage.

The wedding took place before a small congregation of family members at the same time as the Men's final at Wimbledon between reigning champion Italian Jannik Sinner and German Alexander Zverev.

Katie dazzled in a long white gown with her blonde hair swept up as she tied the knot with her partner of six years, Alex, 27, who is the world number five as well as the top-ranked Australian.

She arrived at the church with her husband-to-be – who was smartly dressed in a black suit, white shirt and bow tie – in the front seat of a black Porsche Carrera that he had been driving.

The couple, stepping out untraditionally together before getting hitched, smiled as they walked, bride first and groom behind, before a few well-wishers.

Pictures from the ceremony showed the couple in the stunning Leicester location

The day was bright sunshine for the day

The day was full of celebration and joy for everyone involved

The newlyweds are set to become one of international tennis's most prominent sporting couples.

Katie has been Britain's number one female player for much of the past five years and now stands at number two.

Between them, the pair have earned more than $30million (£22.5million) in career prize money and won an impressive 15 singles titles across the ATP and WTA Tours.

The couple, who announced their engagement in 2024, married in a beautiful Grade II-listed church in Old Woodhouse, Leicestershire, near the village of Woodhouse Eaves where Katie grew up.

A local resident, who knows Katie's parents, said: 'Some people in the village knew the wedding was happening but were sworn to secrecy.

'It's not often two top tennis players get married in your local church, but out of respect for the family we kept it quiet.'

The woman added: 'But a few of us wandered along and stayed in the churchyard where a new wild meadow area has recently been planted.

'We just wanted to see the bride who we've watched growing up in the neighbourhood and we are so proud of her career and achievements.'

Sports.title: Spain star who was attacked by Argentina players in shameful World Cup scenes insists they SHOULDN'T be banned amid FIFA's violent conduct investigation
Sports.content:
Spain star Gavi has surprisingly leapt to the defence of Leandro Paredes despite being involved in a nasty clash with the midfielder following the World Cup final.

Argentina were so close to retaining their title on Sunday after lifting the trophy in 2022, but were beaten 1-0 by Spain after a tense and scrappy affair.

Lionel Scaloni's side were aggressive throughout the match, as they had been during their semi-final victory over England, yet things escalated at the end of the game.

Having already had Enzo Fernandez sent off for a wild late challenge on Pau Cubarsi towards the end of normal time, Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground by putting his hand in the Spaniard's face.

Nahuel Molina also thumped Rodri in the torso as he was running by to celebrate Spain's triumph, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Paredes even appeared to throw punches during the altercations and Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala held Garcia around the throat before he struck Dani Olmo.

Gavi (No 9) leapt to the defence of Leandro Paredes despite their post-World Cup final clash

Paredes was involved in clashes with Spain's players but Gavi said he shouldn't face a ban

Then, as the Spanish squad lifted the trophy, Argentina's players faced away from their opponents in what was viewed by many as a poor show of sportsmanship.

FIFA have since launched an investigation into their behaviour, which could have serious consequences for the players involved.

However, during Spain's celebrations back home, Gavi was asked for his take on the chaos and left many surprised as he called for leniency towards Argentina's stars.

'No, to tell you the truth, I don't think he (Leandro Paredes) should be suspended,' he told Spanish radio station El Partidazo de COPE.

'I understand it's not a good image for children, but I think there's also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

'The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that's it. In the end, I think it's all football, and it has to be that way.'

Paredes was fortunate not to be sent off during the game after committing a series of fouls while he was on a yellow card, and despite some miscommunication, he wasn't dismissed for his role in the post-match chaos.

Despite Gavi's words, Argentina's antics were widely condemned elsewhere, including from BBC Sport's pundits during their coverage of the game.

Micah Richards said: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time. Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Gavi did admit that the full-time scenes on Sunday were 'not a good image for children'

Fellow BBC pundit Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney also gave his views and said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina's players could also face further disciplinary action after FIFA opened an investigation following their semi-final win over England when several of them lifted a controversial banner touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands, which read: 'Las Malvinas Son Argentinas'.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford can play big part in Man Utd's exciting new era - but MUST change
Sports.content:
In his slightly philosophical social media post, Marcus Rashford hit the nail on the head. After spending quality time with his family and friends, Rashford says he will ‘come back a better version' of himself.

And if there is to be a reconciliation with his employers, Rashford needs to be a better version of himself. That means - when he returns to training with Manchester United - being scrupulously professional at all times.

That means matching the work rate of every other player in a reinvigorated United squad. That means selflessness on and off the field.

That also means working assiduously on aspects of his game that still, at the age of 28, need improving. With Michael Carrick having done so well and now in long-term charge, this feels like the start of a new United era.

‌



Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design READ MORE :

And there is no reason why Rashford cannot be a part of it, if he wants to be. New rules agreed between FIFA and FIFPRO, the global players’ union, mean that clubs can no longer have so-called ‘bomb squads’.

If Rashford stays at United - and his contract runs for another two years - he has to be part of the first-team squad. And what Rashford then has to do is prove he is worth his place in the team. Rashford has a lot to prove, as he himself hinted in that social media post.

The cold, hard fact is that Barcelona did not think it was worth paying £26million for his full-time services. The cold, hard fact is that successive England managers have not fully trusted Rashford.

He had a distinctly mixed World Cup - one that was in keeping with his entire England career. Of his 78 caps, 38 have come from the bench.

‌



View 3 Images Marcus Rashford and Michael Carrick have a good relationship (Image: 2020 Soccrates Images B.V.)

Right now, does Rashford get in Carrick’s first-choice starting XI when everyone is fit? You suspect a lot of United supporters would say no.

Is he, for example, a better option than Bryan Mbeumo? Probably not. But he could be - if his focus was complete, if his work rate was stepped up.

Rashford’s numbers in his loan season at Barcelona looked decent enough. In all competitions, 14 goals and 14 assists. But there must have been something that did not fully convince coach Hansi Flick of his worth.

‌



There must have been something that convinced the Barcelona hierarchy they would be better off spending £70million on Anthony Gordon, who also ended the World Cup as Thomas Tuchel’s preferred option. There was also a clause in Rashford’s contract that allowed other clubs - Manchester City and Liverpool excepted - to buy him for £40million, which expired earlier this month.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel ended up preferring Anthony Gordon to Marcus Rashford at the World Cup (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA, The FA via Getty Images)

As expected, no-one triggered that clause. Those scenarios should provoke Rashford into a reaction.

Right now, it is clear the executives at United - headed by director of football Jason Wilcox - would like Rashford’s £325,000-a-week off the books. But they cannot force him out.

‌



And the bottom line is that any interested club will point to the option price Barcelona had and refuse to pay considerably more than that. For want of a better phrase, United could be stuck with Rashford.

But all the interested parties can make that work. Wilcox, Carrick and, most importantly, Rashford himself. If he is true to his promise and comes back from his holiday as a better version of himself, there is no reason he cannot play a key role in United’s new era.

Sports.title: Japan's King George star facing the ‘biggest race of his life’ in £2million Ascot showpiece
Sports.content:
Japan's King George star facing the ‘biggest race of his life’ in £2million Ascot showpiece

Masquerade Ball, pipped by defending champion Calandagan in the Japan Cup last year, has come to Britain to take on the world champion racehorse again

View 4 Images Takahisa Tezuka with Masquerade Ball in Newmarket (Image: Megan Rose Photography)

Japan’s King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes star is facing the ‘biggest race of his life’ in Saturday’s £2 million Ascot showpiece.

‌



Masquerade Ball, pipped by last year’s King George winner Calandagan in the Japan Cup, has come to Britain for a rematch with the world champion racehorse.

‌



He is one of two contenders from Japan with the less heralded Wurttemberg, the mount of Oisin Murphy, also taking his chance. The pair arrived in the UK on July 12 after flying from Tokyo to Amsterdam via Anchorage in Alaska before completing the final leg of the journey by road to Newmarket.

‌



Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone retired after finishing career on a high READ MORE :

Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture READ MORE :

Masquerade Ball is set to clash again with defending champion Calandagan after only a head separated the duo in the G1 Japan Cup in November. On his only start this year Masquerade Ball finished second to Romantic Warrior in Hong Kong’s G1 FWD QEII Cup in April.

Trainer Takahisa Tezuka said: “I have taken care of Masquerade Ball this year. He has matured and developed a lot from three to four, not just mentally but physically as well. He is a lot bigger and stronger. I was nervous about the journey over, but everything went smoothly. The horse seems very happy, while his training is going better than I expected.

“The King George is one of the biggest races in the UK – it is a dream to bring him here. We have tried to give him the best preparation, so we hope for the best while also enjoying the experience because it is an honour to be involved.

‌



View 4 Images Masquerade Ball and Wurttemberg working upsides (Image: Megan Rose Photography)

“This race is the biggest of Masquerade Ball’s life so far. Calandagan is not the only horse we have to think about, even though there was only a head between us in the Japan Cup, because there are a lot of other strong competitors. We are looking forward to seeing how much our horse has developed since then.”

Masquerade Ball’s jockey Christophe Lemaire said in April that the colt has the potential to be ‘one of the greats’ of Japanese racing.

‌



Tezuka added: “I was very happy with those comments. Christophe has ridden many great horses, including Equinox, so it was an honour to hear that from such a great jockey.

View 4 Images Calandagan: named best racehorse in the world in 2025 (Image: PA)

“The horse’s owner Mr [Teruya] Yoshida loves Ascot Racecourse and, from last year, pushed me to challenge for this race. The King George rather than the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe is our main reason for bringing Masquerade Ball to Europe.

‌



“In Japan, the racecourses are very flat with no undulations, so Ascot will be a very different challenge. The downhill section could be quite difficult, as it is hard to imitate running downhill [in his training], but I am hopeful that he will be able to overcome this.

“I initially thought that a mile and a quarter was Masquerade Ball’s best distance. However, as time has gone on, I think a mile and a half is more appropriate for him.”

View 4 Images Hiroshi Miyamoto with Wurttemberg (Image: Megan Rose Photography)

‌



Wurttemberg arrives on the back of a career-best second in the G1 Tenno Sho (Spring) over two miles at Kyoto.

His trainer Hiroshi Miyamoto said: “The owner gave me the choice of two races, the King George or the Goodwood Cup. I chose the King George because it is a highly prestigious and honourable race. For me, it is the number one race in the UK.

“Wurttemberg has good stamina, having raced up to distances of 3,600 metres, and I think Ascot’s mile and a half with the undulations should be suitable for him.

Article continues below

“Oisin Murphy is the number one jockey here, so we are excited for him to ride the horse. He knows Ascot very well and we will rely on him.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury casts doubt over Anthony Joshua fight - 'He's a bottlejob'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury casts doubt over Anthony Joshua fight - 'He's a bottlejob'

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are expected to finally meet in the ring later this year, but the 'Gypsy King' would not be surprised if their clash fails to materialise

View Image Tyson Fury speaks ahead of his return to the ring (Image: @iFLTV/Youtube)

Tyson Fury will not be convinced that Anthony Joshua will fight him until the pair are actually in the ring.

‌



The 'Gypsy King' announced his retirement from boxing last year, only to perform a drastic U-turn just months later. Fury returned to the ring back in April against Arslanbek Makhmudov - and would go on to comfortably beat the Russian powerhouse on points at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

‌



Sitting ringside was Fury's long-time rival Joshua, and the Morecambe scrapper could not resist a pop at 'AJ' - demanding he entered the ring and engaged in a face-off. Fans were left jeering after Joshua refused to accept Fury's request, but the two stars eventually signed a fight contract just days later.

‌



They are expected to trade leather in November, but an official date or venue is yet to be announced. But as the fight edges closer to coming to fruition, Fury still has his doubts and would not be surprised if their mouthwatering clash fails to materialise.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Tyson Fury lashes out at current world champions in blistering rant READ MORE :

During a recent interview with IFL TV, he admitted: "Until that fight happens, walk into the ring... I'm not convinced it does. 100 per cent (on doubts whether the fight will actually happen). I can never see that stiff sitting on the table with me. Ever. What the f*** is he going to say? I can never actually see him at a press conference with me. It will just be like a bombardment. Like I can never see him taking that. He would not even get in the ring.

"I was thinking that the other day. He s*** himself and sat on the stool outside and did not even want to get up and build the fight like make the fight happen. When Turki Alalshikh said to us both 'come on boys, let's do it. Get in the ring and make it happen.' He did not want to do it. So how is he going to come face-to-face at a press conference." He added: "I think he is a bottlejob. A flapper. A chinless wonder as well."

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

While a fight between the pair is expected to take place later this year, they must first get through their respective warm-up fights first. Fury is expected to take on Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand on Friday night, while Joshua will face unknown heavyweight contender Kristian Prenga a day later in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Article continues below

There had been a slight glimmer of hope that Fury would immediately fly over to the Middle East after his fight on Friday and be ringside for Joshua's meeting with Prenga - but that will not be the case. The 37-year-old will instead travel back home, having been away from his wife and children for over two months. "I am going home to the Isle of Man to my wife and kids I've been away from for 10 weeks," he explained.

Sports.title: Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone retired after finishing career on a high
Sports.content:
Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone retired after finishing career on a high

Trainer Alan King called time on his career after collecting the leading chaser prize at the TBA National Hunt Breeders Awards on Tuesday night

View 2 Images Edwardstone: won the 2022 Arkle (Image: Getty Images)

Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone has been retired after finishing his career on a high. The 12-year-old has been one of the stars of Alan King’s stable over eight seasons in which he won 12 times and earned more than £800,000 for owners Robert Abrey and Ian Thurtle.

‌



The decision was taken after Edwardstone was named leading chaser of last season at the TBA National Hunt Breeders Awards on Tuesday.

‌



Edwardstone, who was bred by his owners, showed his potential to go to the top as a novice hurdle when he finished sixth in the Supreme Novices’ Hurdle won by Shishkin.

‌



Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture READ MORE :

Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch READ MORE :

His career took off as soon as he switched to chasing in the 2021-22 campaign when he embarked on a five race winning streak which climaxed in victory in the Arkle Trophy at Cheltenham.

He added three more wins at Grade 1 level, including the 2022 Tingle Creek Chase and, in what was to be his final start in April, in the Celebration Chase.

‌



King said: “The TBA awards was the first time that we had been together since Sandown Park at the end of the season. We had a good chat and we thought retiring Edwardstone was the right thing to do.

View 2 Images Edwardstone: won 12 races and earned more than £800,000 (Image: Getty Images)

“He has had a wonderful career. We have had an awful lot of fun with him and we have had huge success with him. He has retired very fit and well. I hope he has a long, enjoyable retirement as he has been marvellous.

Article continues below

“Winning any Grade 1 is great, but winning the Arkle was terrific. The biggest buzz I probably got from him was when he won the Tingle Creek as it was a hell of a performance. He has been a wonderful horse, and it was great he could finish on a high in the Celebration Chase.

“He will be greatly missed, but he will never be forgotten here at Barbury. I think the plan is for the daughter of one of his owners to have him now. He has got to be kept active, whether it is showing or whatever, but he will enjoy an active retirement.

“My next target now is to find another one like him. It won’t be easy, but we will give it a good try.”

Sports.title: Donald Trump backs Gianni Infantino for shocking new job after FIFA World Cup backlash
Sports.content:
Donald Trump backs Gianni Infantino for shocking new job after FIFA World Cup backlash

Donald Trump is reportedly backing FIFA President Gianni Infantino to become the next United Nations Secretary-General after their high-profile partnership during the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump, President of the United States have formed a close friendship. (Image: (Photo by Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images))

Donald Trump has reportedly given FIFA President Gianni Infantino his backing to become the next United Nations Secretary-General after growing close during their collaboration on delivering the 2026 World Cup. The pair have been thrust into the global spotlight, and the president of the United States is now championing Infantino for the role.

‌



Current Secretary-General, Antonio Guterres, is set to stand down at the end of December 2026, having held the position for nine years, while Infantino has been at the helm of FIFA since 2016. Trump reportedly views Infantino as a unifying figure with worldwide credibility following years of engagement with football leagues, World Cup national associations, and major sponsors.

‌



Trump reportedly believes Infantino would be perfectly suited to the role, according to the New York Post. This comes after a lip reader disclosed Infantino's appeal to Trump that he brushed aside at the World Cup final, and a body language expert identified the motive behind his 'purposeful' stunt.

‌



Amazon founder Jeff Bezos 'approached' as FSG enter talks over Liverpool investment READ MORE :

UEFA president 'boycotts' World Cup final after Donald Trump and FIFA outrage READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Trump's backing for Infantino intensified after the 2026 World Cup concluded, following numerous appearances together during the tournament's closing stages. Infantino could yet pursue a fourth term as FIFA President when his present mandate expires in 2027.

"The World Cup turned out to be a spectacular SUCCESS!" Trump posted on Truth Social after Spain defeated Argentina in the final. He expressed gratitude to law enforcement and others who contributed, and offered particular commendation to Andrew Giuliani and Infantino.

‌



"Few people will ever be able to accomplish what he has done in elevating the World Cup to a level that nobody thought was possible."

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump show off the World Cup winner's medals (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Trump was spotted alongside Infantino following England's semi-final defeat to Argentina and once more during Spain's trophy and medal ceremony.

‌



However, the US President cannot simply hand Infantino the Secretary-General role. According to Article 97 of the UN Charter, the Secretary-General is chosen by the General Assembly following a recommendation from the Security Council.

A member state must first put forward a candidate, who then faces public scrutiny and Security Council straw polls before any formal recommendation can be made.

The primary obstacle is securing a minimum of nine Security Council votes while avoiding a veto from any of the five permanent members: the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, or China.

‌



Trump can lobby and attempt to wield his influence should he pursue this avenue following the New York Post report.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury lashes out at current world champions in blistering rant
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury lashes out at current world champions in blistering rant

The 'Gypsy King' will return to the ring on Friday night against Polish veteran Mariusz Wach, but ahead of the clash, Fury had some harsh words to say about the heavyweight division

View Image Tyson Fury speaks out ahead of his fight with Mariusz Wach (Image: @boxing/Youtube)

Tyson Fury brutally did not hold back in his assessment of the current landscape of the heavyweight division.

‌



The 'Gypsy King' will return to the ring on Friday night - three months after outpointing Arslanbek Makhmudov in front of over 60,000 fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Fury will take on Polish veteran Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand.

‌



Since Fury's return, the heavyweight division has changed immensely. Following Oleksandr Usyk's controversial stoppage win against kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven over in Egypt back in May, the Ukrainian decided to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has sent shockwaves across the sport.

‌



Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Agit Kabayel is recognised as the WBC title holder. Daniel Dubois became a two-time world champion after knocking out Fabio Wardley back in May for the WBO strap, and the IBF belt remains vacant. Following the monumental shift, it now presents Fury with a perfect chance to become a three-time champion.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised READ MORE :

But when asked where he fits into the current picture in the blue ribbon division, Fury did not mince his words. "He does not. All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Article continues below

He added: "I want to just keep busy and do me. I paid the price. I have fought four or five world title eliminators. I fought all the top contenders... champions... unifies and all of that s***. I have earned the right to do what the f*** I want now. Whoever I want to fight from any sport, I can make that fight happen. Because I am the 'GK' and I do what I want."

Whether Fury decides to fight for another world title remains to be seen. The 37-year-old insists he is content with doing whatever he wants. The Morecambe brawler is expected to come away from his fight with Wach unscathed and then take on long-time rival Anthony Joshua in a highly-anticipated all-British dust-up in November.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool transfer priority - 'Not the ideal situation'
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool transfer priority - 'Not the ideal situation'

Liverpool have added Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz to their squad but Andoni Iraola has made it clear that the club still need to add another winger before the new season

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola wants a new winger (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu)

Andoni Iraola has stressed the need for Liverpool to sign a new winger ahead of the new Premier League season following the departure of Mohamed Salah.

‌



The Reds' talisman confirmed back in March that he would leave Anfield a year early and is seemingly poised to complete a move to the Turkish outfit, Besiktas.

‌



While Liverpool have added Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, a winger by trade, they are yet to commit to a deal for a senior replacement to Salah, who plundered 257 goals across his nine-year stay on Merseyside.

‌



Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain has been heavily linked with Liverpool in recent weeks, while the club made inroads into a deal for the impressive Yan Diomande earlier in the summer, only for PSG to emerge as the attacker's preferred destination.

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Iraola has confirmed Liverpool's search for another winger is ongoing, pointing out that wide attack is one area that definitely needs strengthening.

"I think it is difficult to say a number [on how many incomings]. When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola said from Liverpool's pre-season tour of the United States.

‌



"There are obvious situations where we need to sign players. Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyze what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things."

View 2 Images Liverpool have been linked heavily with PSG's Bradley Barcola (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



While Diomande's preference is a move to PSG, progress on a deal to take the Ivory Coast star to Paris has been slow.

If Diomande does swap RB Leipzig for PSG, the move could open the door for Barcola to leave. He is admired by both the Reds and Arsenal, who also want to level up their left attacking options.

The Premier League champions have been forced back into the market after failing to sign their priority transfer target, Morgan Rogers, who completed a £117million move to Chelsea on Tuesday.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
