World.title: Pork and bacon prices expected to fall
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A surplus of pork in South Africa is expected to push prices down, offering some relief to consumers.

Earlier this year, consumers faced the prospect of higher pork prices following outbreaks of African Swine Fever (ASF) and Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD), which disrupted local supply and prompted precautionary imports. However, those imports have now contributed to an oversupply in the market.

Eskort CEO Arnold Prinsloo says pork farm-gate prices have fallen from around R40/kg to approximately R30/kg.

Concerns that the disease outbreaks would significantly reduce local supply led processors to secure imported pork to avoid shortages.

"With imported meat taking between eight and 10 weeks to arrive, the shipments entered the market just as local farms emerged from mandatory disease control restrictions and resumed normal operations," says Prinsloo.

"Consumers will be able to buy pork and bacon at a reduced price," he adds.

Farms affected by FMD were placed under restrictions for a minimum of 42 days after no new symptoms were detected. Prinsloo says that while these measures are essential for controlling the disease, they also create a backlog of market-ready animals that enter the market once restrictions are lifted.

Combined with softer consumer demand following earlier price increases, the result has been a significant oversupply of pork, putting downward pressure on prices.

The lower farm-gate prices are already filtering through to retailers.

"The current market conditions are good news for consumers," says Prinsloo.

"We have ample supply, lower prices and, importantly, no food safety risk to consumers."

World.title: GBV epidemic | Gender Commission aims to improve access to justice
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Commission for Gender Equality is working to develop a practical blueprint that will help people understand how the criminal justice system responds to gender-based violence and femicide cases.

The inquiry is being jointly led by the Human Rights Commission, the Commission for Gender Equality and the CRL Rights Commission, as gender-based violence and femicide remains a national crisis.

Despite policy reforms and government interventions, many survivors continue to face barriers in accessing protection, support services and justice.

Chairperson of the South African Commission for Gender Equality, Nthabiseng Sepanya-Mogale, says the inquiry aims to produce a blueprint that everyone will be able to use to understand what is happening within the criminal justice system in relation to GBVF matters.

She says the inquiry will not begin with victims, survivors or their families, but will instead examine the context in which these forms of violence occur, so that the report captures the enabling environment that society is expected to respond to.

Sepanya-Mogale says the inquiry will then look at how violations arise from that environment and, importantly, how duty bearers respond to them, saying that understanding that response is key to the commission.

World.title: Lithuania moves Red Army graves to leave behind Soviet past
World.content:
VILNIUS - A wartime grave-site outside Lithuania's capital has become the stage for a political skirmish with Russia, as the Baltic country works to shed the last remnants of Soviet occupation.

Sifting through layers of clay-coloured soil, archaeologists in Vievis, west of Vilnius, carefully uncover the bones of Red Army soldiers at one of the many memorial sites installed by Moscow in the wake of the Second World War.

Lithuania removed most Soviet monuments shortly after regaining independence in 1990, but it was not until the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 that Kyiv's close ally Vilnius opted to move the graves -- which many saw as the last visible symbols of USSR domination.

"The memorial site served a propaganda purpose," Tadas Simonauskas, the chief archaeologist on site, told AFP as his team conducted the excavations.

Among the bones, the twisted remains of a gas pipe were the only remnant of an eternal flame installed by the Soviets to memorialise what Moscow still refers to as the "Great Patriotic War".

Used to describe one of World War Two's most significant chapters, as the Allies battled Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front, the term has been rejected by many post-Soviet countries as a distortion of the realities of occupation.

"The memorial stood here to remind us that we were supposedly 'liberated' by the Soviets," Petras Martisius, a local pensioner passing by the dig site, told AFP.

"They should have been moved earlier."

- 'De-Sovietisation' -

Now an EU and NATO member state, Lithuania -- which borders Russia and its ally, Belarus -- fears that it risks being invaded next as the war in Ukraine drags on into its fifth year.

It was shortly after the start of the war that the Lithuanian parliament passed the so-called "de-Sovietisation" law, paving the way for the removal of the last Soviet monuments and the relocation of the graves.

World.title: Australia cricket great Warner pleads guilty to drink-driving
World.content:
SYDNEY - Australia cricket great David Warner pleaded guilty on Wednesday to drink driving and will be sentenced later this year, court documents showed.

Warner, who is one of Australia's best-known sportsmen, was accused of being at the wheel of a van and stopping short of a random testing site, before being breath-tested, arrested and taken to a police station.

His lawyer appeared at a Sydney court to enter a guilty plea on one count of "middle range" drink-driving.

Former opening batsman Warner, who captains Sydney Thunder in the domestic T20 Big Bash League, did not appear in court.

"So many of us make those poor decisions. I think what's important is accepting and being accountable for those poor decisions," lawyer Bobby Hill told a hearing earlier this year.

"It doesn't matter if you're a tradesman, a doctor or one of the best opening batsmen in the world, that danger exists for every one of us."

Warner will be sentenced on August 18.

World.title: 'The Dink' sees comedy in US pickleball craze
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - When filmmaker Josh Greenbaum first ventured onto a pickleball court, he found an accessible pastime that could quickly turn intense, generating not just sweat but a range of emotions in minutes.

His conclusion: pickleball had all the right ingredients for comedy.

Greenbaum drew on that observation to direct "The Dink," an Apple TV film premiering this Friday on the streaming platform.

"I think part of what's so funny about it is, you know, how quickly something that starts very (much) as casual fun can become deeply competitive and also weirdly emotional," the 47-year-old director told AFP in an interview.

"The Dink" brings together Dusty (Jake Johnson) -- a former tennis prodigy who spends his time reminiscing about past glories, much to the chagrin of his father (Ed Harris) —- and Candace (Mary Steenburgen), a divorcee who has developed a passion for pickleball in this new phase of her life.

The film, which features realtime former tennis ace Andy Roddick, is about reinvention, ego, friendship, "and trying to find purpose," Greenbaum said.

World.title: Mbekweni small-scale farmers fighting against evictions
World.content:
PAARL - Mbekweni small-scale farmers say that the Drakenstein Municipality is not engaging them on their plans for them and their livestock.

Municipality spokesperson, Seraj Johaar, says plans are afoot to develop the land on which the farmers occupy for housing. They say, however, there are no immediate plans to evict the over 100 farmers yet.

They do have plans, however, to remove additional structures on the land that they say is for health reasons.

An estimated 200 pigs died from swine flu.

Farmer Norman Mqokolo says that the structures the municipality wants to remove are where the pigs are quarantined so that they do not infect other pigs.

World.title: Check your car: NCC recalls Nissan, Toyota and Lexus vehicles over safety risks
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Consumer Commission (NCC) has announced the recall of all Nissan Qashqai, Toyota Land Cruiser 300 and Lexus LX600.

The NCC says the recall affects 945 vehicles with faults that could pose serious safety risks.

Nissan is recalling 314 Qashqai SUVs over a faulty fuel pipe that could wear over time and potentially cause a fuel leak.

The affected vehicles were sold between 4 May 2021 and 17 September 2024.

Toyota is recalling 507 Land Cruiser 300s while Lexus is recalling 124 LX600s.

The NCC says manufacturing debris inside the engine could lead to engine failure or an unexpected stall while driving increasing the risk of a crash.

The affected Land Cruiser 300s and Lexus LX600s were sold between December 2022 and May 2024.

World.title: eThekwini contractors vow to intensify protest over unpaid work
World.content:
DURBAN - Unpaid water and sanitation contractors in KwaZulu-Natal have vowed to intensify their protest outside the Pinetown depot until their demands are met.

The artisans accuse the eThekwini Municipality of favouritism in public procurement.

They say qualified, experienced contractors are sidelined in favour of companies with little or no plumbing experience, companies allegedly connected to municipal managers.

Contractors, employed by the municipality for over 20 years, say they have not worked since last year.

They accuse the municipality of appointing new plumbing service providers before resolving existing contracts.

They further allege these new contractors lack valid contracts and plan to pay workers below municipal rates.

"We were working perfectly until May and then they just stopped us altogether and they said there is no more work," says water contractor Barry Kid.

Kid says the municipality has not paid since January and, six months later, they still have not been paid.

In a statement, the municipality said the Auditor-General found its previous plumbing contractor system irregular, prompting a new contracting model.

Authorities urge protesting contractors to resolve disputes through legal channels, while the City continues rolling out the new system and maintaining water services.

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Why public servants have less than a month to update pension records
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Public servants given until August 14 to update pension records [File]

Government has directed all public servants to update their records with the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) by August 14, 2026, in the latest step towards modernising pension administration.

In a circular signed by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Capital Development Dr Jane Imbunya, all PSSF members are expected to update their personal information and beneficiary details through the PSSF Member Self-Service Portal or the PSSF Mobile Application.

The circular was addressed to Ministries, State Departments, Constitutional Commissions, Independent Offices, County Public Service Boards and County Governments.

The exercise is expected to streamline pension administration and accelerate the processing of retirement benefits supported by a new Pension Administration System (PAS), a digital platform developed by PSSF to deliver faster, more transparent and more efficient pension services.

The registration exercise targets 529,635 members drawn from across the public service, including 332,950 teachers under the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), 120,084 officers in the disciplined services, 60,322 employees in Ministries, Departments, Constitutional Commissions and Agencies (MDCAs), and 16,279 county government employees.

PSSF Chief Executive Jonah Aiyabei said updating member records is critical to the success of the pension reforms and the delivery of efficient retirement services.

“By updating their records, public servants will enable quicker processing of retirement benefits, reduce administrative delays, improve data integrity, allow members to access pension services seamlessly through digital channels and ensure that the right benefits reach the right beneficiaries at the right time,” he said.

Under the new system, members can access their pension statements in real time, monitor contributions, view projected retirement benefits, update beneficiary nominations and personal details and initiate and track pension claims remotely.

The platform also features a Sponsor Portal that enables employer institutions to submit payroll information, contribution schedules and member data electronically, significantly improving efficiency and accountability in pension administration.

Dr Aiyabei said the Pension Administration System marks a significant milestone in the government’s efforts to digitise pension administration and restore dignity to retirees through faster, more accessible and transparent services.

“It will provide our members with real-time access to their pension information, enable seamless engagement with the Fund and support a fully digital, paperless pension administration process. Ultimately, our goal is to restore dignity in old age by ensuring every public servant receives timely and efficient pension services,” he said.

World.title: Inside Kenya's Ebola defences as seven Americans enter quarantine
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A doctor provides care to a patient with Ebola virus disease at the Rwampara Ebola Treatment Centre (ETC) in Bunia, Ituri, July 13, 2026. [AFP]

Seven American humanitarian workers are spending 21 days under medical observation in Kenya not because they are ill, but because they could become ill.

A Reuters report published today confirms they are seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) staff from the Christian humanitarian organisation Samaritan's Purse . Franklin Graham, the organisation's President and CEO, confirmed this, saying:

“Samaritan's Purse has seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team staff members there. None of them have any symptoms, but they are being quarantined by the Kenyan government for 21 days."

The aid workers, all returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where they were involved in responding to the world's largest recorded outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, have no symptoms and have not tested positive for the virus.

Yet under new US public health rules, they cannot travel home immediately. Instead, they are completing a precautionary quarantine on Kenyan soil.

Their arrival has reignited debate over Kenya's role in regional outbreak preparedness and raised a question that extends far beyond the fate of the seven Americans:

If Ebola crossed Kenya's borders tomorrow, is the country ready?

The answer, infectious disease experts say, lies not in panic but in years of quiet preparation that most Kenyans have never seen.

That preparedness became evident during a recent visit by The Standard to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), where access to one of the hospital's high-security isolation areas was restricted.

Hospital officials informed the reporting team that patients with Mpox were being managed in the unit and, for safety reasons, journalists were not allowed to enter or film inside.

The brief encounter offered a glimpse into the strict infection prevention measures that underpin Kenya's readiness for dangerous infectious diseases.

According to an infectious disease physician at the Kenyatta National Hospital and head of the isolation ward, preparedness is far more than having an isolation room.

"One thing we should never do as Kenyans is panic," he says. "Panic only makes the situation worse. Instead, we should ask ourselves one question: Are we prepared?"

His answer is unequivocal. "As a government and as health institutions, we are in preparedness mode."

Dr Nyukuri explains that preparedness begins long before the first patient arrives at a hospital.

It means evaluating whether enough trained personnel are available, whether laboratories have the necessary testing reagents, whether protective equipment is adequate, and whether health workers understand every step required to safely manage a suspected Ebola patient.

"Here at Kenyatta National Hospital, we have conducted extensive training for healthcare workers," he says. "We have carried out readiness assessments, simulated patient scenarios and practised every stage of care from the moment a suspected patient arrives, through admission, isolation and treatment."

The simulations, he explains, are designed to ensure that no decision is being made for the first time during a real emergency. "When we eventually encounter a suspected case, it should not be something new to us." Dr Duncan Nyukuri, an Infectious Diseases specialist, during an interview with The Standard on July 16, 2026 at Kenyatta National Hospital. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Preparedness also extends beyond hospitals. Health surveillance teams remain stationed at airports and land border crossings, screening travellers arriving from affected regions while rapid response teams stand ready to investigate suspected infections.

"So far, Kenya has done a good job," Dr Nyukuri says. "We have not recorded a confirmed case despite the increasing numbers in the DRC. We pray that remains the case. But if we receive one patient, we are prepared."

How Ebola jumps from animals to people

Although Ebola is often associated with outbreaks, the virus begins its journey quietly in nature.

Dr Nyukuri explains that fruit bats are believed to be the natural reservoir of the virus. "They carry the virus without becoming sick themselves," he says.

Problems arise when increasing human activity brings people into closer contact with wildlife.

Mining, logging, hunting, charcoal burning, expanding settlements and encroachment into forests all increase the likelihood of viruses crossing from animals into humans.

"We call these zoonotic diseases," Dr Nyukuri explains. "Once the virus infects a human being, it can then spread from person to person through contact with infected body fluids, leading to outbreaks within families and communities."

You see, Ebola is a family; many people speak about Ebola as though it were a single virus.

In reality, scientists recognise five different species.

The best known is the Zaire strain, responsible for the devastating West African epidemic between 2014 and 2016.

"It is highly infectious and highly deadly," says Dr Nyukuri. "But because we have studied it extensively, we now have licensed vaccines and effective treatment options."

The Sudan strain, which has repeatedly caused outbreaks in Uganda, is the second most significant.

The current emergency, however, involves the Bundibugyo strain, first identified in Uganda's Bundibugyo District.

"This is the third recorded outbreak caused by Bundibugyo," Dr Nyukuri explains. "We have not studied it nearly as much as the Zaire strain."

There is currently no licensed vaccine specifically targeting Bundibugyo Ebola.

Instead, researchers are evaluating experimental vaccines while clinical trials in eastern DRC are testing promising treatments, including the monoclonal antibody MBP134 and the antiviral drug remdesivir.

"That is why this outbreak concerns many of us," he says. "We still have limited tools compared to what exists for the Zaire strain."

While Kenya has not recorded a confirmed case linked to the current outbreak, neighbouring countries remain on high alert.

Uganda on Thursday declared its last Ebola patient and has begun the mandatory 42-day countdown required before the country can officially be declared Ebola-free.

In contrast, eastern DRC continues battling sustained transmission, placing enormous pressure on treatment centres and frontline health workers.

It is against that backdrop that Kenya has found itself playing an increasingly important role in regional preparedness.

Their presence has nevertheless fuelled public debate over Kenya's preparedness infrastructure and the country's place in global health security.

Earlier this week, two American humanitarian workers who contracted Ebola while working in eastern DRC were medically evacuated to Germany for specialised treatment after receiving initial care in Bunia. Their evacuation underscores an important distinction: Kenya is currently serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed but healthy personnel, while confirmed Ebola patients requiring advanced clinical care have been transferred to Germany.

For Dr Nyukuri, the conversation should remain grounded in science rather than fear.

Preparedness, he says, is not measured only by isolation wards or specialised equipment, but by the ability of an entire health system to detect threats early, respond quickly and protect both patients and healthcare workers.

"My prayer is that Kenya never records a case," he says. "But preparedness means planning for the day you hope never comes."

As seven healthy humanitarian workers quietly complete their quarantine in Kenya, that preparation is no longer an abstract exercise.

It is being tested in real time. The development has also drawn attention to the contrasting roles played by East African countries during the current outbreak.

Uganda, widely regarded as one of Africa's most experienced countries in responding to Ebola, recently brought its own outbreak under control and has now entered the 42-day countdown required to be declared Ebola-free. Over the years, the country has built a reputation for rapidly detecting cases, tracing contacts and isolating patients, earning praise from the World Health Organization for repeatedly containing outbreaks before they spread widely.

Yet despite that experience, Uganda did not become a destination for foreign humanitarian workers requiring precautionary quarantine or post-exposure observation.

Instead, that role has fallen to Kenya, where seven American aid workers are now completing a mandatory 21-day quarantine after working in Ebola-affected areas of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The contrast raises broader questions about how countries are selected to support international outbreak responses. While Uganda has demonstrated its capacity to treat Ebola patients within its own borders, Kenya's involvement appears to reflect a different function—serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed personnel rather than a treatment centre for confirmed cases.

Health experts caution against interpreting the distinction as a measure of either country's clinical capability. Instead, they say such decisions are often influenced by a combination of bilateral agreements, operational logistics, evacuation arrangements and the specific objectives of international public health partners.

World.title: MPs push for urgent resolution of higher education funding crisis
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

HELB Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari before the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education on July 16, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

The National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education has called for urgent and coordinated action to address persistent funding challenges affecting Kenya's higher education sector.

The MPs proposed a joint engagement involving Parliament, the National Treasury and the Ministry of Education to streamline implementation of the Higher Education Funding Model.

The committee, chaired by Vice Chairperson Eve Obara, made the recommendation after holding separate meetings with officials from the State Department for Higher Education, the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) and the Universities Fund during a review of the 2025/2026 Budget Implementation Status.

Appearing before the committee, Higher Education Principal Secretary Dr. Beatrice Inyangala said the Higher Education Funding Model is operational but continues to face implementation challenges due to inadequate alignment between the funding framework and budget allocations.

"The funding model is functional. However, the main challenge lies in budget alignment," Dr. Inyangala told Members.

The funding model was introduced to allocate financial support to university students based on their level of need, while ensuring sustainable financing for public universities.

However, implementation has generated debate over affordability, funding adequacy and delays in disbursement of resources to institutions.

MPs observed that the mismatch between policy and budgetary allocations has undermined effective financing of universities and agreed that a joint meeting involving the National Treasury, the Ministry of Education and Parliament would help harmonise the funding framework.

The committee also sought explanations over the growing stock of pending bills owed by public universities.

Dr. Inyangala informed Members that most of the outstanding obligations were inherited over several years, with universities continuing efforts to clear the debts despite increasing interest charges.

According to the State Department for Higher Education, public universities had accumulated pending bills amounting to Sh100.3 billion as of January 2026.

The ministry said institutions are prioritising settlement of pending obligations, suspending stalled development projects and exploring alternative revenue streams to prevent further accumulation of debt.

During a separate session, Members questioned HELB officials on how the board allocates student loans when available funding cannot meet demand from all eligible applicants.

Led by Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari, HELB officials were asked to explain the criteria used in determining beneficiaries during periods of constrained resources.

Legislators emphasised that the allocation process should be fair, transparent and predictable to protect deserving students from being unfairly excluded.

World.title: High court suspends President Ruto's executive order placing IPOA under Interior Ministry
World.content:
The High Court has temporarily suspended the implementation of president William Ruto's Executive Order No. 2 of 2023 that placed the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) under the Ministry of Interior and National Administration, pending the hearing and determination of a constitutional petition challenging the directive.



Justice David Mburu of the High Court in Milimani law court issued the conservatory orders in a case filed by Jonathan Obwogi under Maalim and associates advocates against the Attorney General, the Cabinet Secretary for Interior and National Administration, and the Independent Policing Oversight Authority.



The court ruled that the contested section of the Executive Order would remain suspended until the constitutional petition is fully heard and determined.



The decision does not amount to a final declaration on the legality of the Executive Order. Instead, the court restored the legal position that existed before the order was issued to safeguard the constitutional issues raised in the petition from further prejudice.



Under Section 4 of the IPOA Act, the authority is required to operate independently and is not subject to the direction or control of any person, office or institution in the performance of its functions. The law further requires all government agencies to assist and protect IPOA's independence, prohibits interference with its decision making and operations, and obligates Parliament to ensure it receives adequate funding.



The conservatory orders mean that the Ministry of Interior cannot, for now, supervise, administer, direct or exercise authority over IPOA based on Executive Order No. 2 of 2023.



The court's decision, however, does not affect IPOA's day-to-day operations. The authority will continue carrying out its statutory mandate, including investigating complaints against police officers, probing deaths and serious injuries arising from police action, and undertaking all responsibilities assigned to it under the IPOA Act.



In the petition, the applicant also sought to compel IPOA's Chairperson, or another authorised officer, to disclose through an affidavit whether the authority had implemented the Executive Order, the extent to which it had operated under the Ministry of Interior, and any operational changes that may have resulted. The petitioner argued that such information would help establish whether the authority's statutory independence had been compromised.



The High Court observed that the question of whether Executive Order No. 2 of 2023 is constitutional will only be determined after hearing submissions from all parties.



The matter is scheduled for a mention on September 21, 2026, when the court is expected to issue further directions.

World.title: Gachagua accuses IEBC of bias ahead of Ol Kalou by-election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Gachagua wants IEBC to commit to conducting the Ol Kalou by-election in a free, fair, and credible manner.

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) of bias and demanded assurances that Thursday's Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election will be conducted in a free, fair and credible manner.

In a letter addressed to IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, Gachagua claimed the commission had lost public confidence and alleged it had selectively enforced electoral laws in favour of the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA).

He cited previous by-elections, including those in Malava, Mbeere North and Narok Town Ward, claiming the commission failed to act against alleged voter bribery, intimidation and violence involving politicians allied to the government.

Gachagua also questioned the commission's handling of disciplinary action against Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia, arguing she had been unfairly treated and denied due process.

The former Deputy President further alleged that senior government officials, including Cabinet Secretaries, Principal Secretaries and other state officers, had actively campaigned for the UDA candidate in Ol Kalou without attracting sanctions from the electoral commission.

He raised concerns about the integrity of the July 16 poll, claiming he had received information from a meeting allegedly held on July 13 that involved UDA officials, government officers and political leaders.

According to Gachagua, discussions at the meeting allegedly centred on plans to interfere with the electoral process.

Among the allegations, he claimed there were plans to delay accreditation of DCP agents, postpone the opening of polling stations in opposition strongholds, issue double ballot papers to UDA supporters, permit voter bribery, deploy plain-clothes police officers to intimidate voters and agents, and interfere with vote counting through planned power outages.

He also alleged that police officers in civilian clothing would be deployed inside polling stations and that additional security personnel would be used to suppress opposition supporters and disrupt vote tallying.

At the same time, Gachagua questioned the commission's decision to rely solely on the electronic voter register, arguing that a manual register should remain available as a backup in line with a 2022 High Court ruling.

The DCP leader urged the IEBC to publicly confirm that all party agents would receive accreditation on time, polling stations would open as scheduled, ballot papers would be properly scrutinised, security agencies would remain impartial and all legal safeguards governing voting and vote counting would be observed.

He also accused police of failing to investigate several alleged incidents targeting DCP supporters and campaign teams in Ol Kalou, including assaults, destruction of campaign equipment and an alleged attempted assassination of former East African Legislative Assembly member Kanini Kega.

He warned that any irregularities in the by-election could undermine public confidence in the IEBC's ability to conduct the 2027 General Election.

"The Ol Kalou by-election is an acid test for the IEBC," Gachagua said, urging the commission to use the poll to restore public trust in Kenya's electoral process.

World.title: Wetang'ula risks jail over alleged breach of court orders on political campaigns
World.content:
National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula addresses residents in Bungoma County. [Bernard Lusigi, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a contempt application seeking to have National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula jailed for at least one month or fined Sh725,017 for each political engagement for allegedly violating conservatory orders issued on July 8, 2026.

Justice David Mburu ordered that a contempt of court application filed by Vocal Africa against Wetang'ula be fast-tracked over allegations that he continued to disobey court orders restraining him from participating in partisan political campaigns, including allegedly campaigning for President William Ruto's re-election.

World.title: Turkish President praises Spain’s humanitarian stance on Palestine
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan praised Spain’s humanitarian stance on the Palestinian issue, adding that it was one greatly appreciated by football fans worldwide.

According to a statement issued by the Turkish Presidency, Erdogan congratulated Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez on Spain’s World Cup victory during a phone call.

He expressed his deep appreciation for the joy of the Palestinians in Gaza who watched the match amidst the rubble following Spain’s triumph.

During the call, on Tuesday, the two leaders discussed bilateral relations and regional and international issues.

Erdogan expressed his gratitude for Sánchez’s attendance at the NATO summit in Ankara on July 7-8.

Erdogan added that he would be pleased to welcome Sánchez back to Turkey in early 2027 for the Turkey-Spain Intergovernmental Summit, which is expected to witness the signing of new agreements and the strengthening of bilateral cooperation in several sectors.

World.title: Egypt condemns any threats targeting Saudi Arabia’s security
World.content:
Egypt strongly condemned any threats targeting the security of Saudi Arabia, which undermines the security and stability of the region and threatens the safety of maritime navigation, international trade, and vital waterways.

In a statement issued by the Foreign Ministry, Egypt affirmed that these threats constitute a flagrant violation of international law, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and relevant Security Council resolutions.

Egypt stressed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and all the Gulf Cooperation Council states, and its support for all measures they take to preserve their security, stability, sovereignty, and territorial integrity.

It emphasized the importance of prioritizing political and diplomatic solutions and respecting the rules of international law, in order to maintaining peace within the region.

World.title: Has Egypt’s government shut down loan apps?
World.content:
An informed source at the Financial Regulatory Authority denied social media speculations on Egypt’s government closing the branches of a large number of non-banking financial companies and institutions.

In a statement to the Middle East News Agency, the source explained that the decision circulating on social media dates back to October 2025, and only involved the cancellation of microfinance licenses for a number of Category C NGOs and institutions.

The source emphasized that the names mentioned on those anonymous social media accounts have no connection whatsoever to the previous decision.

He urged citizens to carefully verify information and consult the proper official channels before sharing information on social media.

World.title: Prosecution closes investigations into unofficial AI-generated Messi and Salah GEM video
World.content:
The Haram Prosecution Office on Tuesday has moved to close investigations into the creation of an AI-generated Lionel Messi and Mohamed Salah video at the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM), and to dismiss any suspicion of a crime against the video’s author, graphic designer Abdel-Rahman Khaled.

The case dates back to a report filed by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities denying any connection to the video, which had been widely circulated on social media platforms – to much confusion.

This led to the arrest of the designer at his residence in Cairo.

Khaled faced accusations of publishing unauthorized visual content infringing on intellectual property rights.

The prosecution’s decision to close the case came after technical examinations and investigations revealed “the absence of criminal intent on the part of the accused, and that the video did not cause any material or moral harm to official bodies or public figures.”

The decision indicated that the work was simply an example of a hobbyist showcasing digital skills without any financial gain.

World.title: Labor Minister meets Indian Ambassador to expand cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Labor Hassan Raddad held talks on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, with Indian Ambassador to Egypt Suresh K. Reddy on expanding cooperation in vocational training, employment and investment.

During the meeting, held at the ministry’s headquarters in the New Capital, Raddad said that Egypt and India continue to strengthen their long-standing relationship, particularly following the elevation of bilateral ties to a strategic partnership.

The minister added that the two sides discussed cooperation in labor mobility, vocational training, particularly in advanced technology fields, and occupational safety and health.

He also proposed partnerships between Egyptian and Indian technology training centers to help prepare skilled workers for the changing needs of local and international labor markets.

The minister said the ministry is committed to facilitating procedures in accordance with national regulations while supporting a competitive investment environment.

He also welcomed a proposal to hold a meeting with Indian companies operating in Egypt to discuss labor regulations and address any challenges they may face.

For his part, Reddy reaffirmed India’s interest in expanding cooperation with Egypt, particularly in the economic and industrial sectors, and invited Raddad to visit India for talks on strengthening cooperation in labor, employment and vocational training.

World.title: Egypt receives 22 tons of French medical aid for Palestinian patients
World.content:
Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar received on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, a new 22-ton shipment of medical aid from the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.

The shipment includes medicines, medical supplies and equipment to support Egyptian hospitals treating Palestinian patients and wounded people.

Abdel Ghaffar said the shipment reflects the strategic partnership between Egypt and France and their shared commitment to humanitarian support for Palestinians, adding that French assistance since the start of the Gaza crisis has included medical care, humanitarian aid and treatment for critical cases in French hospitals.

French Minister Delegate for Francophonie, International Partnerships and French Nationals Abroad Éléonore Caroit praised Egypt’s role in treating around 100 wounded Palestinians daily, saying the new shipment will help strengthen Egyptian hospitals’ capacity to provide medical care and ease the suffering of civilians in Gaza.

Abdel Ghaffar also highlighted the broader Egypt-France health partnership, which extends to primary healthcare, universal health insurance, maternal and child health programs and the treatment of Palestinian children with cancer.

World.title: Egypt’s ambassador to Cameroon presents credentials as non-resident envoy to Central African Republic
World.content:
Egypt’s Ambassador to Cameroon Marwa Hegazy presented on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, her credentials to Central African Republic President Faustin-Archange Touadéra as Egypt’s non-resident ambassador to the Central African Republic.

Following the ceremony, Hegazy met with President Touadéra, who asked her to convey his greetings to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and praised Egypt’s efforts to support security and stability in his country.

The Central African president stressed the importance of continued cooperation and building on shared values to serve the interests of his country.

For her part, Hegazy affirmed Egypt’s commitment to supporting efforts to achieve peace and development in the Central African Republic and its readiness to provide various forms of support in priority areas.

She also highlighted the role played by Egyptian troops participating in the UN peacekeeping mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) in promoting stability and preserving peace and security, particularly in the capital, Bangui.

The ambassador expressed her aspiration to coordinate with Central African government officials in a manner that serves the interests of the two brotherly peoples.

World.title: PM reviews efforts to strengthen investment climate in Sinai
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, government efforts to strengthen the investment climate in the Sinai Peninsula, stressing the importance of attracting diversified investment to support development, create jobs and make better use of the region’s economic potential.

These remarks came during Madbouly’s meeting with senior officials. The participants outlined a package of measures introduced to encourage investment, including incentives for investors, regular reviews of challenges facing companies operating in Sinai and legislative updates aimed at supporting business activity.

The meeting also reviewed progress in simplifying investment procedures, including the establishment of an Investor Services Center in South Sinai, where representatives of relevant government agencies provide licensing and approval services.

Additionally, Madbouly was also briefed on coordination between the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and the National Authority for the Development of the Sinai Peninsula, which has helped speed up the processing of investment applications and reduce approval times.

World.title: Two ZANACO ATM Custodians Arrested Over K1 Million Theft
World.content:
Police in Lundazi District, Eastern Province, have arrested two ATM custodians at the ZANACO Lundazi Branch in connection with the alleged theft of more than K1 million.

The suspects, Melinda Longwa (42) and Jessy Phiri (29), are facing allegations of theft by servant after K1,000,050 reportedly went missing from the bank’s ATM room.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba said the suspected theft was uncovered during a surprise cash inspection conducted by Branch Manager McDonald Milambo Mutambwa before the custodians were due to load K1,000,600 into the ATMs.

According to Mr. Mweemba, the inspection revealed a discrepancy of K1,000,050 between the cash expected and the amount found in the ATM machines. A reconciliation carried out by ZANACO ATM operations specialists from the bank’s head office confirmed that the general ledger balances did not match the physical cash count.

When questioned, the two suspects reportedly claimed they had accidentally swapped ATM cash cassettes on an earlier date, placing K100 notes in a cassette meant for K500 notes. They alleged this resulted in customers withdrawing more money than intended.

The suspects further told investigators they failed to report the error because they feared losing their jobs.

Police have since detained the pair as investigations into the matter continue.

World.title: State House Accuses Opposition of Recycling Government Policies
World.content:
State House has accused the opposition of failing to present original policy alternatives ahead of the elections, saying its campaign is largely based on programmes already being implemented by the government.

In a statement issued to the media, State House Chief Communications Specialist Clayson Hamasaka said the opposition has not offered a distinct vision for Zambia’s development, but has instead echoed government initiatives across several key sectors.

Mr. Hamasaka said the opposition’s campaign messages mirror existing government policies in mining, energy, agriculture, manufacturing, education, healthcare and public sector recruitment, rather than introducing fresh proposals.

He claimed the only notable new proposal put forward by the opposition is the distribution of excavators to marketeers operating in trading places across the country.

Mr. Hamasaka further stated that the opposition had the opportunity to implement its own policies while in government but instead left behind economic challenges, including high debt levels, weakened institutions and reduced investor confidence.

He also accused the opposition of resorting to personal attacks on President Hakainde Hichilema after failing to provide credible policy alternatives.

According to Mr. Hamasaka, by adopting programmes already being implemented by the government, the opposition is effectively endorsing President Hichilema’s development agenda. He added that calls for a policy debate are difficult to justify without a clearly distinct policy platform from the opposition.

World.title: ZCCM-IH, Ministry of Mines Discuss Establishing Gold Markets
World.content:
ZCCM Investments Holdings (ZCCM-IH) is in discussions with the Ministry of Mines on plans to establish gold trading markets in areas where gold mining is being formalised.

ZCCM-IH Board Chairperson Phesto Musonda says the initiative is aimed at supporting the formalisation of Zambia’s gold and manganese mining sectors, in line with the government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s mining industry.

Mr. Musonda described the proposed markets as a key part of the government’s broader economic agenda, saying they will help create structured and transparent trading opportunities for small-scale miners.

He further revealed that the Ministry of Mines has so far trained local miners and issued mining licences to between 700 and 1,000 cooperatives, particularly in gold-rich areas such as Mufumbwe.

The initiative is expected to improve market access for miners, encourage legal trade, and boost economic growth through increased participation in the formal mining sector.

World.title: ZDA’s Investment Deal Room attracts 202 investors seeking financing
World.content:
The Zambia Development Agency (ZDA), says its newly launched Zambia Investment Deal Room has attracted 202 investors seeking financing for projects across key sectors of the economy.

Speaking during a media briefing in Lusaka today, ZDA Director General, Albert Halwampa said the digital platform, which became operational in mid-June this year, is connecting investors with local and international financiers to unlock funding for investment projects.

Mr Halwampa disclosed that 187 investment projects submitted through the platform are currently at various stages of review.

He further said 28 fund providers, comprising banks, development finance institutions and institutional investors, have already joined the platform to finance projects in sectors such as agriculture, mining, energy, manufacturing, tourism infrastructure and other priority industries.

Mr Halwampa explained that while ZDA has continued issuing investment licences to prospective investors, many projects fail to materialise because investors struggle to secure financing.

“The Zambia Investment Deal Room was developed to bridge this gap by providing a digital marketplace where investors seeking capital can directly engage with potential financiers from Zambia and around the world,” he added.

Mr Halwampa said investors and funding institutions that have already registered on the platform have begun engaging each other and discussing possible investment transactions, expressing optimism that successful deals will soon be concluded.

He also urged Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), artisanal miners, local entrepreneurs and large-scale investors to take advantage of the platform to access financing and grow their businesses.

Mr Halwampa further encouraged banks, development finance institutions and other investment funds to register on the platform and support the financing of commercially viable projects.

He described the Zambia Investment Deal Room as a long-term digital solution that is expected to transform investment financing in Zambia by improving access to capital and increasing the implementation rate of licensed investment projects.

World.title: Simuuwe denies FRA fraud claims, reports Mwamba to police over ‘false’ publications
World.content:
Simuuwe denies FRA fraud claims, reports Mwamba to police over ‘false’ publications

United Party for National Development Media Director Mark Simuuwe has dismissed allegations linking him, President Hakainde Hichilema and several other individuals to the fraudulent acquisition of maize from the Food Reserve Agency, describing the claims as false, malicious and defamatory.

In a statement issued on 22 July, Mr Simuuwe said neither he nor the President had fraudulently obtained maize from the agency or failed to meet any payment obligations as alleged in publications circulating on social media. He said the allegations form part of what he described as a coordinated disinformation campaign intended to mislead the public and damage the reputations of those named.

Mr Simuuwe also rejected documents circulating online that purport to link him to the matter, including material said to originate from the Zambia National Service, saying they were fabricated and should not be regarded as authentic. He disclosed that the matter has been reported to the Zambia Police Service for investigation, arguing that the publication and circulation of false information and fabricated documents may constitute offences under the Cyber Security Act of 2025 and other applicable laws.

He further confirmed that he has separately reported former diplomat Emmanuel Mwamba to police over what he described as a series of false and malicious online publications. According to Mr Simuuwe, the complaints include allegations concerning his academic qualifications, including claims that he never attended the University of Zambia, as well as publications relating to the Food Reserve Agency and the Zambia National Service, which he maintains are false.

Mr Simuuwe stated that he holds two degrees from the University of Zambia, and accused those behind the publications of deliberately spreading misinformation about his background and business dealings.

He warned that anyone found to have originated, knowingly shared or republished false information in breach of the Cyber Security Act and other laws could face legal action, and urged members of the public to verify information before sharing it on digital platforms. “Freedom of expression should not be used to justify the publication of falsehoods or fabricated documents,” he said.

Mr Simuuwe expressed confidence that law enforcement agencies would investigate the matter thoroughly and ensure that anyone found responsible is dealt with in accordance with the law.

The denial follows the earlier circulation of correspondence between the Zambia National Service’s Chongwe Milling Plant and a company associated with Mr Simuuwe, which showed an outstanding balance for mealie meal supplied on credit and a subsequent proposal to repay it in instalments. Mr Simuuwe’s statement disputes the authenticity of documents linked to that matter, though it does not specifically address the correspondence in detail.

Mr Mwamba has not yet issued a public response to Mr Simuuwe’s complaint. Neither the Zambia Police Service nor the Zambia National Service has commented publicly on the status of any investigation. The matter remains unresolved, with both the underlying allegations and Mr Simuuwe’s denial yet to be tested through any formal process.

World.title: Northern Service Delivery Charter launched
World.content:
The Provincial Administration in Northern Province has launched the province’s service delivery charter.

The Service Delivery Charter guarantees accessible, efficient and responsive public services for the local communities.

Speaking when she unveiled the document during the second quarter Provincial Development Coordinating Committee (PDCC) meeting in Kasama district yesterday, Northern Province Acting Permanent Secretary Beauty Undi-Phiri urged public service officers to align their operations with the charter’s guidelines and ensure that services are delivered in a manner that responds to the needs of the people.

Ms Undi-Phiri highlighted the significant milestones achieved by the government since taking office in 2021, citing decentralisation as a major development.

She noted that the province has recorded notable progress during this tenure pointing out the increase in Constituency Development Fund (CDF), allocation from K1.6 million to K40 million, which she said has empowered communities to implement projects that respond to local needs.

“This year marks a significant milestone as we reflect on the five years of implementing the United Party for National Development government’s vision as outlined in the manifesto and the 8th National Development Plan. During this period the province has recorded notable progress including the increased CDF from K1.6 million to K40 million,” she said.

“Government has spearheaded the constitution amendments that have seen an increased number of constituencies following the delimitation exercise which will result in increased allocation of the Constituency Development Funds in 2027, progress in the agriculture, education and health sectors, among others,” she added.

And Northern Province Dean of District Commissioners Risto Mushembe, who spoke through Kaputa District Commissioner Cosmas Mwaya, called for teamwork and shared commitment to achieve the objectives outlined in the development plan.

Mr Mushembe noted that enhanced coordination will enable the province to accelerate service delivery and improve the socio-economic wellbeing of the people.

“I want to thank you for coming and for your continued commitment and dedication to the development of our province, through your active role in this important coordination platform.” Mr Mushembe said.

He reminded public service workers to uphold the civil service code of ethics by remaining professional, upholding integrity, accountability, impartiality and respect in the execution of duties.

He added that these values are fundamental to promoting public confidence and ensuring the delivery of quality services to the citizens.

The charter sets clear service standards guided by values of accountability, honesty, professionalism, impartiality, transparency and inclusivity.

World.title: Vice President urges civil servants to implement policies
World.content:
Vice President Mutale Nalumango has advised civil servants in Mwansabombwe district to continue implementing government policies.

Speaking when she addressed civil servants at Kapale secondary school assembly hall, the vice president said public servants are the implementing wing of the government.

She said public servants are interconnected and if one fails to function, the whole chain breaks down.

The Vice President who once again visited Mwansabombwe district on her continued tour of Luapula province also paid a courtesy call at the Mwata’s palace.

She said everyone is part of the government and each one has a role to play for the smooth implementation of government programmes.

She advised civil servants to familiarise themselves with the ruling party’s manifesto for them to understand the vision of the party.

“Policies are found in the political party manifesto. You should not feel ashamed to have a UPND manifesto on your tables. You should acquire and read the manifesto of the ruling party so that you can understand it for you to implement the government policies effectively,” She advised.

She said understanding the policy of the government will help civil servants to interpret and implement government programmes.

Meanwhile, the Vice President said the current reduced power load management was not political but assured that it will be sustained beyond the elections because the government has invested heavily in power generation.

“Government has done a mix of power generation. in addition to hydro, we have also invested in solar and thermal energy to improve on power generation,” the vice president said.

The Vice President further called for unity, hard work, equity, transparency and accountability among civil servants so that development can be achieved.

And when she met the clergy, she asked the clergy to continue spreading messages of peace and unity as the country goes to the polls on August 13, 2026.

She said everyone had a responsibility to pray for those in government authority so that both can live a peaceful life.

“All leadership is from God. As children of God, you have the responsibility to pray for us in leadership and pray for the nation as a whole,” Dr. Nalumango said.

The Vice President advised the clergy to pray as they go to cast their votes on August 13, 2026 so that they can vote wisely.

The Vice President informed the clergy that the government is improving the welfare of the vulnerable through social protection programmes like social cash transfer.

She said from the time the UPND government took office, the number of social cash transfer beneficiaries has increased and many vulnerable people in the communities are benefiting.

She further said the introduction of free education which is now law has enabled many poor people to go back to school.

Meanwhile, members of the clergy appreciated the government for the various developmental projects being implemented countrywide.

Charles Mpundu who represented the clergy said the introduction of free education has seen thousands return to school.

Reverend Mpundu said many families who previously struggled to send their children to school can now educate their children giving them hope again.

He also appreciated the government for increasing the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) which has brought development closer to the people.

“Through CDF, schools, roads, water projects, health facilities, market shelters, youth and women empowerment are being supported,” he said.

He however requested the government to consider working on the Mansa-Nchelenge Road and upgrading the township roads and feeder roads.

World.title: ZRA Intercepts Seven Somali Nationals Hidden Under Rice Bags
World.content:
The Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) has intercepted seven Somali nationals who were allegedly being smuggled through Zambia to Zimbabwe after they were found concealed beneath bags of rice in a vehicle during a routine operation in Kapiri Mposhi.

According to ZRA, officers stopped a Toyota Probox travelling towards the Chirundu One Stop Border Post and, upon inspection, discovered the seven immigrants hidden in the rear cargo compartment under bags of rice and other goods.

The Zambian driver of the vehicle, together with the seven Somali nationals, was handed over to the Department of Immigration for profiling and further legal action in accordance with the Immigration and Deportation Act.

Meanwhile, in a separate enforcement operation, ZRA impounded a motor vehicle that had remained in Zambia illegally after its temporary import permit expired.

The authority said the vehicle entered the country through Kasumbalesa Border Post in December 2025 but was not re-exported after the permit lapsed, in violation of customs regulations.

ZRA has since reminded importers and motorists to comply with customs laws, warning that failure to do so may result in enforcement measures, including the seizure of vehicles and goods.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - July 22, 2026
World.content:
Ghana Opposition Slams 20-Year Illegal Mining Sentence

Ghana's opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has condemned the conviction of its Ashanti regional chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as "Chairman Wontumi", after he was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment with hard labour for illegal mining offences. Boasiako has been convicted of granting mineral rights without approval and facilitating unlicensed mining through his company, Akonta Mining. He is the first senior Ghanaian politician to be convicted since the government's crackdown on illegal mining began in 2017. The NPP has said the verdict is politically motivated and it will appeal. Environmental campaigners have hailed the conviction as a major step in holding powerful people accountable for illegal mining, which has caused widespread environmental damage across Ghana.



Nigerian Officers Arrested Over Alleged Extortion of Anti-Graft Chief

Four Nigerian police officers are facing disciplinary action after allegedly setting up an illegal checkpoint in Abuja to extort money from motorists, including the head of the country's anti-corruption agency. Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission chairman Musa Aliyu alleged that the officers stopped him and forced him to withdraw $38 from an ATM after threatening to take him to court over a supposed traffic offence. Following Aliyu's complaint, police launched an operation that led to the officers' arrest. The Commissioner of Police, Ahmed Sanusi, said that the alleged abuse of power will not be tolerated, and officers who commit criminal acts will have no place in the police service.

Senegal Backs Macky Sall's UN Chief Bid

President of Senegal, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, has endorsed former President Macky Sall's bid to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations. It is a major turnaround in the relations between the two leaders. The endorsement follows a meeting between Faye and Sall and comes despite years of political tensions after Sall's controversial presidency and the 2024 election that brought Faye to power. Faye has instructed his government to rally support for Sall's bid as "Senegal's candidacy in the service of Africa." The decision has drawn criticism from opposition figures, civil society groups and victims' families, who argue Sall's record of alleged political repression makes him unsuitable for the UN's top post.

DR Congo Battles Fastest-Growing Ebola Outbreak

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is battling its fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with 2,423 confirmed cases, 967 deaths and 469 recoveries reported as of 19 July. The outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo virus variant, has spread across five eastern provinces, with Ituri accounting for more than 90% of infections and 80% of deaths. The World Health Organization (WHO) warned that ongoing insecurity, population displacement and the absence of an approved vaccine or treatment are hampering efforts to contain the disease. In some areas, including Kisangani, rapid response actions have helped stop further spread. Early detection, contact tracing and community engagement remain central to the response.

144 Migrants Dead or Missing Off Mauritania Coast

The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has said that at least 144 migrants are dead or missing after a series of maritime tragedies off the coast of Mauritania. Many of the migrants, including refugees, had spent 25 days stranded at sea after departing from The Gambia headed for Spain's Canary Islands. Rescue efforts culminated in an operation on 18 July where teams found 38 survivors and 143 dead or missing. Among the survivors that day were two children who lost their entire families at sea. UNHCR said the tragedy highlights the urgent need for safer legal migration pathways. It urged countries to consider "meaningful and quicker access to legal pathways through higher resettlement quotas, increased labour opportunities and education pathways as alternatives to the dangerous sea crossings."

Close 

Africa Now World's Hunger Hotspot, UN Warns

A new United Nations report has found that global hunger declined for the third consecutive year in 2025. But Africa has become the epicentre of the world's food crisis and the continent now has the largest number of hungry people worldwide. The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026 report estimates that 645 million people globally went hungry last year. Two-thirds of Africans could not afford a healthy diet and more than half suffered moderate or severe food insecurity. The global number of hungry people decreased by almost 14 million compared with 2024 and by 43 million since 2022. The UN warned that progress remains fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal of ending hunger by 2030. The UN warned that conflict, climate shocks and declining humanitarian funding continue to threaten progress. The group urged governments to invest in resilient food systems and make nutritious diets more affordable.

World.title: South Africa: Power Utility Eskom Says Koeberg Remains Safe - South African News Briefs - July 22, 2026
World.content:
Eskom Reassures Public After Koeberg Radiation Incidents

Eskom has assured the public that there is no danger to people or the environment following three radiological contamination incidents at Koeberg Nuclear Power Station's Unit 2 during maintenance between June 30 and July 7, reports EWN. The utility said the low levels of radioactive contamination were contained within the reactor building and that no radioactive material was released outside the facility. Eskom's Chief Nuclear Officer, Velaphi Ntuli, said the incidents were safely managed under strict protocols and do not affect the National Nuclear Regulator's decision to extend the operating life of Unit 2 by 20 years.

UK Murder Suspect Returns to Johannesburg Court

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

British-Zimbabwean national Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma is set to appear in the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court after his case was postponed for legal status verification and address checks, reports SABC News. The 45-year-old was arrested in Johannesburg on July 10 after police found him in possession of an unlicensed 9mm firearm. He is also wanted in the United Kingdom in connection with the alleged murders of his wife and two daughters. South African authorities are processing a provisional extradition request while he first faces the local firearm charge.

Matlala Trial Continues as Witness Resumes Testimony

The trial of alleged criminal kingpin Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala and his four co-accused continues in the High Court in Johannesburg, reports SABC News. The first State witness is expected to resume cross-examination. The accused face 25 charges linked to three alleged attempted assassinations between 2022 and 2024, including those of taxi boss Joe "Ferrari" Sibanyoni, Tebogo Thobejane and DJ Vettys. Security officer Bethwell Cele testified that gunmen armed with AK-47 rifles opened fire on Sibanyoni and his entourage at a golf estate before also shooting at him during the attack.
